description: Editorial study labels for the Torah Law records: form (Jewish division into positive and negative commandments) and category (traditional Christian division into moral, ceremonial and civil law). The site's classification field is separate and unchanged.

form.Positive: Requires an action, a procedure, or a status or penalty to be applied (mitzvat aseh).
form.Permission: Allows an action without requiring it.

category.Moral: A duty of love toward God or neighbour, stated as right or wrong in itself.
category.Ceremonial: A rite or holiness rule of Israel's worship under the old covenant.
category.Civil: A rule for Israel as a nation: its courts, penalties, government, land and economy.

ceremonial_area.Sacrifice and offerings: Sacrifices, offerings, tithes, firstfruits and firstborn animals for the altar.
ceremonial_area.Priesthood and sanctuary: Priests, Levites, the high priest, the tabernacle and its holy things.
ceremonial_area.Dietary laws: Clean and unclean animals, blood, fat, carcasses and other food prohibitions.
ceremonial_area.Ritual purity: Impurity and cleansing: corpses, skin disease, discharges, childbirth.
ceremonial_area.Festivals and holy days: Sabbath rites, new moons, the annual feasts, and the sacred side of the sabbatical year and Jubilee.
ceremonial_area.Signs, vows and dedications: Circumcision, tassels, mixed kinds, vows, Nazirites, valuations and devoted things.

definitions.form_mixed: True when the provision holds both a requirement and a prohibition; form gives its main clause.
definitions.maimonides_613: Maimonides' commandments (Sefer HaMitzvot numbering) matched to the record in the Torah Law count check, carried to current IDs.

records.title: Reckon the Exodus month as the first month of the year
records.form_basis: "it shall be the first month" (12:2)

records.title: Slaughter the Passover at the prescribed time and location
records.form_basis: "shall slaughter it toward evening" (12:6)

records.title: Do not eat the Passover animal raw or boiled
records.form_basis: "You shall eat none of it raw" (12:9)
records.note: Mixed: the verse also requires roasting ('but roasted with fire'); main clause, per title and 613 match N125, is the ban on eating it raw or boiled.

records.title: Do not leave Passover meat until morning
records.form_basis: "You shall leave none of it until morning" (12:10)
records.note: Exodus 12:10 prohibits leaving the meat overnight. Its conditional requirement to burn any remainder has its own catalogue record, C0100, so this overnight ban is a single negative provision.

records.title: Do not break a bone of the Passover
records.form_basis: "you shall not break a bone of it" (12:10)

records.title: Keep the Passover memorial throughout the generations
records.form_basis: "You shall celebrate it as a feast" (12:14)

records.title: Eat unleavened bread during the appointed seven days
records.form_basis: "For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread" (12:15)
records.note: Not mixed: the leaven removal and leaven-eating ban in this verse are separate records (C0109, C0106).

records.title: Do not eat leaven during the seven-day feast
records.form_basis: "whoever eats leaven … that soul shall be destroyed" (12:15)

records.title: Hold the appointed holy assemblies on the first and seventh days of Unleavened Bread
records.form_basis: "The first day shall be called holy" (12:16)
records.note: Not mixed: the work ban in the same verse is recorded separately (C0108).

records.title: Do no prohibited work on the first and seventh days, with the stated food exception
records.form_basis: "You shall do no servile work on them" (12:16)
records.note: Not mixed: besides the work ban the verse adds only a permission (food preparation); the P 613 matches (rest) match the holy-day clause recorded in C0107.

records.title: Remove leaven from Israelite houses for the seven-day feast
records.form_basis: "you shall remove leaven out of your houses" (12:15)
records.note: Mixed: 12:19 adds the prohibition 'no leaven shall be found in your houses' (N201); main clause, per title, is the duty to remove leaven (P156).

records.title: Observe the Passover night as a vigil for the Lord
records.form_basis: "a vigil for the Lord … throughout their generations" (12:42)

records.title: Apply the stated circumcision and participation rules for the Passover meal
records.form_basis: "No uncircumcised person shall eat of it" (12:48)
records.note: Mixed: verses 44 and 48 also require circumcising slaves and a foreigner's males before they eat; main clause is the eating ban on outsiders and the uncircumcised.

records.title: Keep the Passover meat within the house where it is eaten
records.form_basis: "shall not take any … meat outside the house" (12:46)
records.note: Mixed: also 'It shall be eaten in one house' (requirement); main clause, per title and 613 match N123, is the ban on taking meat outside.

records.title: Apply the same prescribed law to native and resident foreigner
records.form_basis: "There shall be one law for the native" (12:49)
records.note: The equal-law rule governs Passover participation after circumcision in Exodus 12:43–49. Ceremonial describes its direct scope. Civil captures equal legal treatment of native and resident participants.

records.title: Consecrate the firstborn males to God
records.form_basis: "Consecrate to Me every firstborn" (13:2)
records.note: Covers human and animal firstborn; area follows the firstborn given to God (613 match P79). Redemption of sons is recorded separately (C0119).

records.title: Keep all leaven out of sight within your borders for the seven days
records.form_basis: "no leavened thing shall be seen with you" (13:7)
records.note: Not mixed: the verse's 'eat unleavened bread' clause is a separate direction, as the context note says.

records.title: Redeem the firstborn donkey as prescribed
records.form_basis: "you shall exchange for a sheep" (13:13)
records.note: The firstborn donkey is redeemed, not offered on the altar, so the area follows redemption rather than offerings.

records.title: Redeem firstborn sons
records.form_basis: "Every firstborn of man … you shall redeem" (13:13)

records.title: Keep the seventh day as a holy Sabbath rest
records.form_basis: "Tomorrow is a Sabbath, a holy rest" (16:23)
records.note: Title is the weekly Sabbath rest (Moral, Ceremonial second per brief), but the verse's manna-day baking instructions could read as a detailed rite; N320 is implied, not stated.

records.title: Have no other gods
records.form_basis: "You shall have no other gods" (20:3)

records.title: Do not make idols or images for worship
records.form_basis: "You shall not make for yourself an idol" (20:4)

records.title: Do not bow down to other gods
records.form_basis: "You shall not bow down to them" (20:5)

records.title: Do not serve other gods
records.form_basis: "neither shall you serve them" (20:5)

records.title: Do not misuse God's name
records.form_basis: "You shall not take the name … in vain" (20:7)

records.title: Do ordinary work in six days and rest on the seventh
records.form_basis: "You shall do no work on it" (20:10)
records.note: Mixed: 'For six days you shall labour' frames the schedule; the operative rest clause is the work ban (N320), so Negative.

records.title: Honour father and mother
records.form_basis: "Honour your father and your mother" (20:12)

records.title: Do not commit adultery
records.form_basis: "You shall not commit adultery" (20:13)

records.title: Do not steal
records.form_basis: "You shall not steal" (20:14)

records.title: Do not murder
records.form_basis: "You shall not murder" (20:15)

records.title: Do not bear false witness against your neighbour
records.form_basis: "You shall not bear false witness" (20:16)

records.title: Do not covet your neighbour's wife
records.form_basis: "You shall not covet your neighbour’s wife" (20:17)

records.title: Do not covet your neighbour's possessions
records.form_basis: "You shall not covet your neighbour’s house" (20:17)

records.title: Do not build God's stone altar with hewn stones
records.form_basis: "you shall not build with hewn stones" (20:25)

records.title: Do not ascend the altar by steps exposing nakedness
records.form_basis: "You shall not go up by steps" (20:26)

records.title: Release the Hebrew servant after six years under the stated household conditions
records.form_basis: "he shall go out free, without payment" (21:2)

records.title: A Hebrew servant may choose to remain under the prescribed procedure
records.form_basis: "His master shall pierce his ear" (21:6)
records.note: Title frames the servant's choice as an option, but the verse's operative words prescribe the master's procedure (tribunal, ear-piercing) once he elects to stay.

records.title: Provide redemption for the betrothed servant woman rejected by her master
records.form_basis: "he shall redeem her" (21:8)
records.note: Not mixed: the ban on selling her to foreigners (21:8) is recorded separately (C0167).

records.title: Do not sell the rejected servant woman to foreigners
records.form_basis: "he has no right to sell her" (21:8)
records.note: A servant-law rule (Civil); its stated ground, 'he has broken faith with her', gives it a clear moral character, so Moral second.

records.title: Treat a servant woman betrothed to the master's son according to a daughter's rights
records.form_basis: "he shall deal with her … for daughters" (21:9)

records.title: Do not deprive the servant wife of her necessities
records.form_basis: "he shall not deprive her of her necessities" (21:10)

records.title: Do not deprive the wife of her clothing
records.form_basis: "he shall not deprive her … her clothing" (21:10)

records.title: Do not deprive the wife of conjugal companionship
records.form_basis: "he shall not deprive her … conjugal companionship" (21:10)

records.title: Release the servant wife without payment when her stated rights are withheld
records.form_basis: "she shall go out freely, without silver" (21:11)

records.title: Remove the deliberate murderer from sanctuary protection for judgment
records.form_basis: "you shall take him from My altar" (21:14)

records.title: Execute the person who strikes father or mother
records.form_basis: court penalty: "shall surely be put to death" (21:15)
records.note: Record is the court penalty (audience: authorities), so Positive; 613 match N319 is the underlying prohibition on striking a parent.

records.title: Apply the prescribed death judgment for reviling father or mother
records.form_basis: court penalty: "shall surely die" (21:16)
records.note: Record is the court penalty (audience: authorities), so Positive; 613 match N318 is the underlying prohibition on cursing a parent.

records.title: Execute the kidnapper who enslaves or sells the victim
records.form_basis: court penalty: "he shall surely die" (21:17)

records.title: Compensate the injured person's lost labour and healing costs
records.form_basis: "he shall pay for his lost labour" (21:19)

records.title: Apply the stated judgment when a master fatally beats a slave
records.form_basis: court penalty: "he shall surely be avenged by judgment" (21:20)
records.note: Not mixed: 21:21's 'he shall not be avenged' limits the penalty rather than forbidding an act.

records.title: Impose the assessed fine for the pregnancy injury described in this verse
records.form_basis: "he shall surely be fined" (21:22)

records.title: Apply the prescribed proportionate life-and-injury judgment
records.form_basis: "he shall give life for life" (21:23)

records.title: Release the servant whose eye or tooth the master destroys
records.form_basis: "he shall set them free for their eye" (21:26)

records.title: Stone the ox that fatally gores a person
records.form_basis: court penalty: "the bull shall surely be stoned" (21:28)
records.note: Not mixed: the ban on eating the ox's flesh (21:28) is recorded separately (C0183).

records.title: Do not eat the flesh of the condemned goring ox
records.form_basis: "its flesh shall not be eaten" (21:28)
records.note: A food prohibition, so Ceremonial (Dietary laws) per brief; Civil second because it belongs to the goring-ox judgment the site classes as civil.

records.title: Apply the negligent owner's death liability or imposed ransom for a known dangerous ox
records.form_basis: court penalty: "its owner also shall die" (21:29)
records.note: Owner's culpable negligence after warning makes the death a capital wrong, so Moral second; the rule itself is court liability.

records.title: Pay the prescribed compensation when an ox kills a slave
records.form_basis: "he shall give thirty didrachmas of silver" (21:32)

records.title: Compensate the owner of an animal lost in an uncovered pit
records.form_basis: "the owner of the pit shall make restitution" (21:34)

records.title: Settle loss caused by an ox killing another ox, distinguishing prior knowledge of danger
records.form_basis: "they shall sell the living bull and divide" (21:35)

records.title: Make the prescribed restitution for stolen property, with the stated multiples
records.form_basis: "he shall repay five calves for the calf" (21:37)

records.title: Distinguish the stated night and daylight liabilities when a burglar is killed
records.form_basis: status rule: "he is guilty; he shall die in return" (22:2)

records.title: Sell the thief unable to pay the required restitution
records.form_basis: court penalty: "let him be sold for the theft" (22:2)

records.title: Repay double when the stolen animal is found alive with the thief
records.form_basis: "he shall repay them double" (22:3)

records.title: Compensate for damage caused by grazing another person's field or vineyard
records.form_basis: "he shall repay from his own field" (22:4)

records.title: Compensate for fire damage caused to another person's crops or land
records.form_basis: "he who kindled the fire shall make restitution" (22:5)

records.title: A thief caught stealing entrusted goods repays double
records.form_basis: "he shall repay double" (22:6)

records.title: Require double restitution from the convicted party in the property dispute
records.form_basis: "Whoever is convicted … shall repay his neighbour double" (22:8)

records.title: Accept the keeper's exonerating oath without demanding restitution
records.form_basis: "The owner shall accept it" (22:10)
records.note: Not mixed: 'he shall not make restitution' is an exemption from liability, not a prohibition.

records.title: Apply the keeper's restitution liability for theft and the exemption for proved wild-animal loss
records.form_basis: "he shall make restitution to its owner" (22:11)
records.note: Not mixed: 'he shall not make restitution' (22:12) is an exemption from liability, not a prohibition.

records.title: Apply the stated borrower liability and owner-present or hire exceptions
records.form_basis: "he shall make restitution" (22:13)
records.note: Not mixed: 'he shall not make restitution' (22:14) is an exemption from liability, not a prohibition.

records.title: Pay the prescribed marriage payment for seducing an unbetrothed virgin, subject to her father's refusal
records.form_basis: "he shall surely give the marriage payment" (22:15)

records.title: Execute the practitioner of sorcery
records.form_basis: court penalty: "You shall not preserve sorcerers alive" (22:17)
records.note: A court penalty, but phrased as a prohibition ('shall not preserve … alive'); Negative per the operative words and 613 match N310.

records.title: Execute the person who has sexual relations with an animal
records.form_basis: court penalty: "you shall surely put to death" (22:18)

records.title: Apply the prescribed destruction to the person sacrificing to other gods
records.form_basis: court penalty: "shall surely be destroyed" (22:19)

records.title: Do not mistreat or oppress the resident foreigner
records.form_basis: "you shall not ill-treat a resident foreigner" (22:20)

records.title: Do not mistreat the widow or orphan
records.form_basis: "You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan" (22:21)

records.title: Do not press a poor borrower harshly
records.form_basis: "you shall not press him hard" (22:24)

records.title: Do not charge interest to a fellow Israelite
records.form_basis: "neither shall you lay interest upon him" (22:24)

records.title: Return the poor debtor's covering pledge by sunset
records.form_basis: "you shall restore it to him" (22:25)

records.title: Do not revile the 'gods' named in the Saints text
records.form_basis: "You shall not revile gods" (22:27)
records.note: 'Gods' may mean God (blasphemy) or judges (613 match N315); either way a prohibition of a wrong act, so Moral.

records.title: Do not speak evil of the rulers of your people
records.form_basis: "neither shall you speak evil of the rulers" (22:27)

records.title: Do not delay the prescribed firstfruit offerings
records.form_basis: "You shall not delay the firstfruits" (22:28)
records.note: Not mixed: the verse's second clause (give the firstborn of your sons) is a separate provision.

records.title: Give the firstborn animal to God on the eighth day, after seven days with its mother
records.form_basis: "on the eighth day you shall give it" (22:29)

records.title: Do not eat flesh torn by wild animals and throw it to the dogs
records.form_basis: "shall not eat flesh taken by wild animals" (22:30)
records.note: Mixed: also 'throw it to the dog' (disposal directive); main clause, per 613 match N181, is the ban on eating torn flesh.

records.title: Do not accept or circulate a false report
records.form_basis: "You shall not receive an empty report" (23:1)

records.title: Do not follow the crowd into wrongdoing
records.form_basis: "You shall not join the many in evil" (23:2)
records.note: 613 match P175 (majority rule) rests on a rabbinic reading; this verse's wording is wholly prohibitive, so not mixed.

records.title: Do not pervert justice
records.form_basis: "neither shall you … turn aside judgment" (23:2)
records.note: This record selects the second clause in Exodus 23:2 about turning aside judgment. It governs witnesses or judgments as well as personal integrity, matching the Civil overlap used for judicial corruption in C0225.

records.title: Do not favour the poor in judgment
records.form_basis: "Neither shall you favour a poor man" (23:3)
records.note: Exodus 23:3 expressly prohibits favoritism in judgment, so its judicial role is as explicit as the Moral/Civil counterpart against favoring the powerful in Leviticus 19:15 (C0611).

records.title: Return your enemy’s straying ox or beast of burden
records.form_basis: "you shall surely turn it back" (23:4)

records.title: Help raise an enemy’s animal fallen under its load
records.form_basis: "you shall raise it up together with him" (23:5)
records.note: Mixed: also 'you shall not pass it by' (N270); main clause, per title, is the duty to raise the animal with its owner.

records.title: Do not pervert the justice due to the poor in his cause
records.form_basis: "You shall not pervert the judgment" (23:6)
records.note: Exodus 23:6 concerns judgment of the poor in a specific legal cause, in addition to its moral duty of impartiality. Compare the Moral/Civil labels for the parallel prohibition on perverting judgment in Deuteronomy 24:17.

records.title: Keep away from a false accusation
records.form_basis: "shall keep far away from every unrighteous charge" (23:7)
records.note: The 'unrighteous charge' in Exodus 23:7 sits with acquittals, executions and judicial gifts, and the catalogue identifies people bringing or judging charges. Retain Positive for the direct 'keep far away' wording, with medium confidence because it functions as avoidance.

records.title: Do not execute the innocent or righteous
records.form_basis: "the innocent … you shall not kill" (23:7)
records.note: The Moral protection of innocent life also specifically limits Israel's judges and execution authorities in the catalogue and legal context of Exodus 23:7. Civil is a clear secondary category.

records.title: Do not accept bribes or acquit the guilty for gifts
records.form_basis: "you shall receive no gifts" (23:8)
records.note: Bribe-taking and unjust acquittal are moral wrongs; addressed to those judging, so Civil second. 'Keep far away' is an avoidance duty, not a separate requirement.

records.title: Cultivate and gather the land's produce during the six working years
records.form_basis: "you shall sow your land" (23:10)
records.note: 'You shall sow' sets the six working years beside the seventh-year release: an allowance, not a duty (as with six days' labour). Positive is the alternative reading.

records.title: Let the land rest in the seventh year
records.form_basis: "you shall grant it release, and leave it" (23:11)
records.note: Land rest is the sabbatical year's core observance, so Ceremonial second. N220 (no sowing) is implied by 'leave it', not stated, so not mixed.

records.title: Leave sabbatical-year produce available to the specified people and animals
records.form_basis: "leave it; and the poor … shall eat" (23:11)
records.note: Produce left for the poor and wild beasts parallels the harvest provisions for the poor: Civil with Moral second.

records.title: Do not invoke the names of other gods
records.form_basis: "Do not call to mind … other gods" (23:13)
records.note: 'Keep everything I have said' is a general exhortation, not a separate requirement, so not mixed.

records.title: Observe the three pilgrim feasts and the required appearances before God
records.form_basis: "you shall keep a feast to Me" (23:14)

records.title: Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread
records.form_basis: "Keep the feast of unleavened bread" (23:15)
records.note: The verse's empty-handed clause is a separate record (C0232), so not mixed.

records.title: Do not appear before God empty-handed
records.form_basis: "You shall not appear before Me empty-handed" (23:15)
records.note: Concerns the gift brought when appearing at the feasts, hence Sacrifice and offerings; the verse's feast-keeping clause is a separate record (C0231).

records.title: Keep the Feast of Harvest or Weeks
records.form_basis: "you shall keep the feast of harvest" (23:16)

records.title: Keep the Feast of Ingathering or Booths
records.form_basis: "you shall keep … the feast of completion" (23:16)

records.title: Do not offer the sacrificial blood with leaven
records.form_basis: "you shall not sacrifice … with leaven" (23:18)

records.title: Do not leave the feast's sacrificial fat until morning
records.form_basis: "neither shall the fat … remain until morning" (23:18)

records.title: Bring the firstfruits of the land to God's house
records.form_basis: "You shall bring the firstfruits" (23:19)
records.note: 613 match N187 belongs to the verse's milk clause, a separate record (C0238), so not mixed.

records.title: Do not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk
records.form_basis: "You shall not boil a lamb" (23:19)
records.note: The verse's firstfruits clause is a separate record (C0237), so not mixed.

records.title: Do not imitate the nations' idolatrous practices
records.form_basis: "nor do according to their works" (23:24)
records.note: Exodus 23:24 records both a ban on imitating idolatry and a duty to destroy the cult objects. The latter has its own catalogue record, C0242, and belongs to the conquest setting. C0241 covers only the prohibition.

records.title: Make no covenant with the Canaanite peoples or their gods
records.form_basis: "You shall make no covenant with them" (23:32)
records.note: A treaty ban in the conquest is Civil; 'nor with their gods' adds an idolatry ban, so Moral second. Moral primary is the alternative.

records.title: Do not let the specified peoples remain in Israel’s land
records.form_basis: "neither shall they dwell in your land" (23:33)
records.note: Residence ban in the conquest is Civil; idolatry is its stated motive, not its content, so no Moral second, though Maimonides files N51 under idolatry.

records.title: Supply pure beaten olive oil for the sanctuary light
records.form_basis: "to bring you pure beaten olive oil" (27:20)

records.title: Priests: maintain the sanctuary lamps from evening to morning
records.form_basis: "Aaron and his sons shall burn it" (27:21)

records.title: High priest: wear the sounding robe when ministering in the sanctuary
records.form_basis: "Aaron’s sound shall be heard when he ministers" (28:35)

records.title: Priests: wear the covering undergarments when entering or ministering
records.form_basis: "Aaron and his sons shall wear them" (28:43)

records.title: Give the appointed sacrificial portions to the priests
records.form_basis: priestly portion: "shall belong to Aaron and to his sons" (29:28)

records.title: Transfer the high priest's holy garments to his successor
records.form_basis: succession: "Aaron’s holy robe shall belong to his sons" (29:29)

records.title: Do not allow outsiders to eat the consecration meal
records.form_basis: "An outsider shall not eat them" (29:33)
records.note: Exodus 29:33 requires the consecrated priests to eat and separately forbids outsiders to eat. C0329 records the outsider restriction. The positive duty addresses the priests.

records.title: Do not eat the consecration leftovers after the appointed time
records.form_basis: "it shall not be eaten" (29:34)
records.note: C0331 forbids eating the leftovers in Exodus 29:34. Burning the remainder is a distinct positive duty and already has its own catalogue record, C0330.

records.title: Offer the daily morning and evening lambs with the prescribed grain, oil and wine
records.form_basis: "shall offer on the altar: two year-old lambs" (29:38)

records.title: Burn the prescribed incense morning and evening
records.form_basis: "Aaron shall burn finely ground compounded incense" (30:7)

records.title: Do not offer unauthorized incense on the incense altar
records.form_basis: "You shall not offer other incense" (30:9)

records.title: Do not use the incense altar for burnt or grain offerings
records.form_basis: "shall not offer … an offering, or a sacrifice" (30:9)

records.title: Do not pour libations on the incense altar
records.form_basis: "you shall not pour a libation on it" (30:9)

records.title: Make the annual blood purification of the incense altar
records.form_basis: "Once a year Aaron shall make expiation" (30:10)

records.title: Give the equal prescribed census ransom for each counted adult male
records.form_basis: "each shall give the Lord a ransom" (30:12)
records.note: 'The rich shall give no more and the poor no less' fixes the equal amount within the duty; not a separate prohibition, so not mixed.

records.title: Priests: wash hands and feet before sanctuary entry or altar ministry
records.form_basis: "shall wash their hands and feet with water" (30:19)

records.title: Do not apply holy anointing oil to unauthorized persons
records.form_basis: "It shall not be applied to human flesh" (30:32)

records.title: Do not reproduce holy anointing oil for private use
records.form_basis: "you shall not make anything like it" (30:32)

records.title: Do not reproduce the holy incense for personal enjoyment
records.form_basis: "You shall not make incense for yourselves" (30:37)

records.form_basis: "See that you keep My Sabbaths" (31:13)
records.note: A restatement of the weekly Sabbath, so Moral with Ceremonial second per the tie-breaker; its framing as Israel's covenant sign could support Ceremonial primary.

records.title: Execute the Sabbath profaner under Israel's prescribed judgment
records.form_basis: court penalty: "shall surely be put to death" (31:14)
records.note: Court penalty: Civil, Moral second (Decalogue Sabbath, Moral per tie-breaker); Ceremonial is the alternative second. Work is barred only through the penalty clauses, so not mixed.

records.title: Do not kindle fire in your dwellings on the Sabbath
records.form_basis: "You shall not kindle a fire" (35:3)
records.note: 613 match N322 is the rabbinic court-execution reading of this verse; the plain text forbids kindling fire. A detailed Sabbath rite, so Ceremonial per the tie-breaker.

records.title: Present a burnt offering of the prescribed eligible animals or birds
records.form_basis: "he shall bring an unblemished male" (1:3)

records.form_basis: "his gift shall be fine flour" (2:1)

records.note: Saints Translation says 'you shall bring them', but as an exception to 2:11 it allows leaven and honey as firstfruits, not requiring them. Positive is the alternative reading.

records.title: Include the covenant salt with every offering
records.form_basis: "every gift … shall be seasoned with salt" (2:13)
records.note: Also forbids omitting it: 'You shall not let the salt of the covenant … cease' (N99).

records.title: Prepare a first-produce grain offering with roasted groats, oil and frankincense
records.form_basis: "shall bring the sacrifice of the first produce" (2:14)

records.title: Present an unblemished animal of the prescribed kinds for a peace or deliverance offering
records.form_basis: "he shall bring it unblemished before the Lord" (3:1)

records.title: Do not eat the prohibited fat of cattle, sheep or goats
records.form_basis: "you shall eat neither any fat" (3:17)

records.title: Bring the prescribed sin offering for an inadvertent offence, according to the offender's standing
records.form_basis: "he shall bring … an unblemished calf" (4:3)

records.title: Disclose relevant testimony when solemnly called as a witness
records.form_basis: duty to testify: "if he does not declare it" (5:1)
records.note: Guilt for withholding testimony makes testifying a duty, as P178 counts it; truthful witness is also a moral duty, so Moral second.

records.title: Confess the offense in the stated witness, impurity, or oath cases
records.form_basis: "he shall confess the sin" (5:5)
records.note: Confessing sin to God is a lasting duty toward God; here it opens the sliding-scale offering rite (5:6), so Ceremonial second. Ceremonial primary is the alternative.

records.title: Bring the prescribed offering for the stated witness, impurity and oath offences, with poverty substitutions
records.form_basis: "he shall bring unto the Lord" (5:6)

records.title: Add neither oil nor frankincense to the flour sin offering
records.form_basis: "He shall pour no oil upon it" (5:11)
records.note: The flour-bringing clause (5:11a) belongs to the sliding-scale offering with poverty substitutions (C0411); this record is the oil and frankincense ban, so not mixed.

records.title: Give the flour sin offering remainder to the priest
records.form_basis: priestly portion: "what remains shall be the priest’s" (5:13)

records.title: Bring the prescribed guilt ram for misuse of holy things
records.form_basis: "he shall bring … an unblemished ram" (5:15)

records.title: Repay misused holy property with an added fifth
records.form_basis: restitution: "he shall repay … and add a fifth part" (5:16)
records.note: Restitution is Civil, matching the site label; the property is holy and repaid to the priest beside the guilt offering, so Ceremonial second. Ceremonial primary is arguable.

records.title: Bring the prescribed guilt ram for the unrecognized offence
records.form_basis: "he shall bring … an unblemished ram" (5:18)

records.title: Restore the wrongfully retained property and add a fifth upon acknowledgment or conviction
records.form_basis: restitution: "he shall return the plunder which he seized" (5:23)
records.note: Restitution for theft, fraud and false oath: Civil, with Moral second because the underlying acts are moral wrongs.

records.title: Bring the prescribed guilt ram for dishonest dealings and false oaths
records.form_basis: "he shall bring … an unblemished ram" (5:25)

records.title: Keep the altar fire burning continually without quenching it
records.form_basis: "fire of the altar shall burn upon it" (6:2)
records.note: Also forbids quenching it: 'and shall not be quenched' (N81).

records.title: Do not bake the priests' grain offering portion with leaven
records.form_basis: "It shall not be baked with leaven" (6:10)
records.note: Also requires eating the remainder unleavened in a holy place (6:9), the positive side of the same rule.

records.title: Burn a priest’s grain offering entirely and do not eat it
records.form_basis: "and shall not be eaten" (6:16)
records.note: Also requires burning it wholly. The title leads with burning, but N138 and the contrast with eaten grain offerings make the ban the main clause.

records.title: Eligible priests: eat the designated sin offering in the holy court
records.form_basis: "priest who offers it up shall eat it" (6:19)
records.note: N145 (not outside the court) is implied by 'eaten in a holy place'; the verse states no prohibition, so not mixed.

records.title: Do not eat the sin offering whose blood was brought inside the sanctuary
records.form_basis: "none of the offerings … shall be eaten" (6:23)
records.note: Also requires burning them: 'they shall be burned with fire.'

records.title: Eligible priests: eat the guilt offering in a holy place
records.form_basis: "Every male among the priests shall eat them" (7:6)
records.note: N145 is implied by 'in a holy place'; the verse states no prohibition, so not mixed.

records.title: Give the burnt offering hide to the officiating priest
records.form_basis: priestly portion: "the priest … shall have the hide" (7:8)

records.title: Give oven- and pan-cooked grain offerings to the officiating priest
records.form_basis: priestly portion: "shall belong unto the priest who brings it" (7:9)

records.title: Share grain offerings prepared with or without oil equally among Aaron's sons
records.form_basis: priestly portion: "shall belong unto all the sons of Aaron" (7:10)

records.title: Bring the prescribed breads with the thanksgiving peace offering
records.form_basis: "shall bring with the sacrifice of praise loaves" (7:12)

records.title: Eat the thanksgiving peace offering that day and leave none until morning
records.form_basis: "they shall leave none of it until morning" (7:15)
records.note: Also states the deadline positively ('shall be eaten on the day'). The title leads with eating; the operative limit is the leave-none ban, as N120 counts it.

records.title: Eat vow or freewill peace-offering meat within two days
records.form_basis: "third day, it shall not be accepted" (7:18)
records.note: This record sets the permitted eating window and excludes the third day. The required action in 7:17 is disposal, indexed separately as C0452. An eating permission plus a prohibition does not make the record mixed.

records.title: Do not eat sacrificial flesh that has touched uncleanness
records.form_basis: "touches any unclean thing shall not be eaten" (7:19)
records.note: Also requires burning the defiled flesh ('it shall be burned with fire'); 'Whosoever is clean shall eat flesh' allows clean persons to eat.

records.title: Do not eat the holy peace offering while unclean
records.form_basis: prohibition by penalty: "while his uncleanness is upon him … shall perish" (7:20)
records.note: Prohibition expressed by the cutting-off penalty ('that soul shall perish'), as N129 counts it.

records.title: Do not eat the fat of animals found dead or torn
records.form_basis: "it shall in no wise be eaten" (7:24)
records.note: Also permits using such fat for work ('may be used for any work'); a permission, so not mixed.

records.title: Allot the right foreleg to the priest who presents the blood and fat
records.form_basis: priestly portion: "shall have the right foreleg as his portion" (7:33)

records.title: Priests: drink no wine or strong drink when entering the tent or approaching the altar
records.form_basis: "You shall drink no wine or strong drink" (10:9)

records.title: Priests: distinguish holy from profane and clean from unclean
records.form_basis: "to distinguish between the holy and the profane" (10:10)

records.title: Priests: teach Israel God's statutes
records.form_basis: "you shall instruct the sons of Israel" (10:11)

records.title: Eat the breast and foreleg in a holy place with your household
records.form_basis: "shall eat the breast … in a holy place" (10:14)

records.title: Do not eat land animals excluded by the prescribed hoof and cud criteria
records.form_basis: "You shall not eat their flesh" (11:8)
records.note: 11:2–3 permits animals with both signs ('you may eat'), which Maimonides counts as positive P149; a permission, so not mixed. The operative ban is 11:4, 8.

records.title: Do not touch the prohibited animal carcasses
records.form_basis: "You shall not … touch their carcasses" (11:8)
records.note: The verse forbids touching ('shall not … touch'); 613 match P96 reflects Maimonides counting carcass impurity as a positive status law rather than a ban on touching.

records.title: Do not eat water creatures lacking fins and scales
records.form_basis: "You shall not eat their flesh" (11:11)
records.note: 11:9 permits finned and scaled creatures ('you may eat'), which Maimonides counts as positive P152; a permission, so not mixed. 'You shall abhor' reinforces the ban.

records.title: Do not eat the prohibited birds listed in the law
records.form_basis: "they shall not be eaten" (11:13)

records.title: Do not eat prohibited winged insects, observing the stated locust exceptions
records.form_basis: "winged creeping thing … is an abomination for you" (11:20)
records.note: Ban by 'abomination' wording; 11:21–22 permits leaping locusts ('you may eat'), which Maimonides counts as positive P151. A permission, so not mixed.

records.title: Observe the prescribed uncleanness until evening after carcass contact
records.form_basis: status rule: "shall be unclean until evening" (11:24)

records.title: Apply the stated carcass-contamination rules to objects, food, water, and seed
records.form_basis: status rule: "falls when dead shall become unclean" (11:32)

records.title: Do not eat or defile yourselves with the prohibited ground-creeping creatures
records.form_basis: "it shall not be eaten" (11:41)
records.note: 'You shall be holy' (11:44) is the motive for the bans, not a separate requirement, so not mixed.

records.title: Observe the prescribed uncleanness and purification periods after childbirth
records.form_basis: status rule: "she shall be unclean seven days" (12:2)
records.note: 12:4's bans on touching holy things and entering the sanctuary are separate records (C0481, C0482), so not mixed.

records.title: Do not touch holy things during postpartum purification
records.form_basis: "She shall touch nothing holy" (12:4)
records.note: 613 match N129 reads 'touch nothing holy' as a ban on eating holy food; the form agrees.

records.title: Do not enter the sanctuary before postpartum purification is completed
records.form_basis: "shall not enter the sanctuary" (12:4)

records.title: Bring the prescribed childbirth purification offerings, including the poverty provision
records.form_basis: "she shall bring unto the priest" (12:6)

records.title: Declare skin and scalp lesions clean or unclean by their prescribed criteria
records.form_basis: "shall examine him and declare him unclean" (13:3)

records.title: Observe the prescribed public signs while the lesion remains unclean
records.form_basis: "shall put a covering about his mouth" (13:45)

records.title: A person with the unclean lesion: dwell apart outside the camp while the lesion persists
records.form_basis: "he shall dwell apart" (13:46)

records.title: The recovering person: remain outside your house for seven days after camp re-entry
records.form_basis: "shall remain outside his house for seven days" (14:8)

records.title: Present the prescribed eighth-day purification offerings and oil, with the poverty substitutions
records.form_basis: "on the eighth day he shall take" (14:10)

records.title: Determine whether the house lesion is clean or unclean by the applicable signs
records.form_basis: "the priest shall enter to examine the house" (14:36)

records.title: Demolish the house with the persistent lesion
records.form_basis: "they shall demolish the house" (14:45)

records.title: Observe uncleanness until evening after entering the isolated house
records.form_basis: status rule: "shall be unclean until evening" (14:46)

records.title: Apply the stated uncleanness periods and contact rules for bodily discharges
records.form_basis: status rule: "his flow is unclean" (15:2)

records.title: Remain unclean until evening after the specified discharge contact
records.form_basis: "shall wash his garments, bathe in water" (15:5)

records.title: Treat a donkey saddle ridden by a man with the specified discharge as unclean until evening
records.form_basis: status rule: "shall be unclean until evening" (15:9)

records.title: Count seven clear days after the specified discharge ceases
records.form_basis: "he shall count seven days for his cleansing" (15:13)

records.title: Bring the two prescribed birds to the priest after recovery from the discharge
records.form_basis: "he shall take two turtledoves" (15:14)

records.title: Observe uncleanness until evening after the stated seminal emission or intercourse
records.form_basis: "he shall bathe his whole body in water" (15:16)

records.title: Wash semen-contaminated garments or skins and keep them unclean until evening
records.form_basis: "shall be washed with water" (15:17)

records.title: Observe the seven-day menstrual status and its stated contact consequences
records.form_basis: status rule: "she shall remain in her menstrual discharge" (15:19)

records.title: Treat a prolonged or irregular flow of blood as menstrual uncleanness
records.form_basis: status rule: "she shall be unclean" (15:25)

records.title: Count seven days after a prolonged flow ceases before cleansing
records.form_basis: "she shall count seven days" (15:28)

records.title: Bring two turtledoves or pigeons to the priest on the eighth day
records.form_basis: "she shall take two turtledoves" (15:29)

records.title: High priest: do not enter within the veil at unauthorized times
records.form_basis: "let him not enter at all times" (16:2)

records.title: Provide the prescribed personal and congregational animals for the Day of Atonement
records.form_basis: "shall enter the holy place: with a calf" (16:3)

records.title: Keep others out of the tent during the high priest's atonement entry
records.form_basis: "no one shall be in the Tent" (16:17)
records.note: Title is phrased positively, but the verse's operative words are a prohibition: no one may be in the Tent during the atonement entry.

records.title: Humble yourselves on the appointed Day of Atonement
records.form_basis: "humble your souls" (16:29)
records.note: N196 (no eating) is the fast's negative side, drawn from 23:29; this verse states only 'humble your souls'. Its 'you shall do no work' is C0569.

records.title: Do no work on the Day of Atonement
records.form_basis: "you shall do no work" (16:29)
records.note: P164 (rest) is the positive counterpart ('sabbath of rest', 16:31); this verse only forbids work. Its 'humble your souls' is C0568.

records.title: The anointed successor high priest: perform the prescribed annual atonement for the sanctuary, priests and people
records.form_basis: "The priest whom they anoint … shall make atonement" (16:32)
records.note: Area judgment: the high priest's duty, in holy garments, to atone for the sanctuary; it is equally the annual Day of Atonement rite (Festivals and holy days).

records.title: Bring the prescribed sacrifices to God's appointed sanctuary
records.form_basis: "they shall bring them unto the Lord" (17:5)
records.note: Mixed: the passage also condemns slaughtering outside without bringing the animal to the Tent (N90), under cutting-off.

records.title: Do not sacrifice to the vain or demonic objects of worship
records.form_basis: "they shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices" (17:7)

records.title: Do not eat blood
records.form_basis: "No soul among you shall eat blood" (17:12)

records.title: Cover the hunted animal's blood with earth
records.form_basis: "shall pour out the blood and cover it" (17:13)

records.title: Carcass eaters must wash and bathe and remain unclean until evening
records.form_basis: "shall wash his garments and bathe in water" (17:15)
records.note: Concerns the impurity and washing after eating a carcass, not a ban on eating it, so Ritual purity rather than Dietary laws.

records.title: Do not follow the practices of Egypt or Canaan
records.form_basis: "You shall not follow the practices" (18:3)
records.note: In context (18:24-30) the practices are the sexual and idolatrous abominations listed, hence Moral; read broadly as separation from gentile customs (N30), it could be Ceremonial.

records.title: Do not approach close kin for prohibited sexual relations
records.form_basis: "No person shall approach any relative" (18:6)

records.title: Do not uncover your father's nakedness
records.form_basis: "You shall not uncover your father’s nakedness" (18:7)

records.title: Do not have sexual relations with your mother
records.form_basis: "you shall not uncover her nakedness" (18:7)

records.title: Do not have sexual relations with your father's wife
records.form_basis: "not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife" (18:8)

records.title: Do not have sexual relations with your sister or half-sister
records.form_basis: "you shall not uncover her nakedness" (18:9)

records.title: Do not have sexual relations with your granddaughter
records.form_basis: "you shall not uncover their nakedness" (18:10)

records.title: Do not have sexual relations with your paternal aunt
records.form_basis: "not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister" (18:12)

records.title: Do not have sexual relations with your maternal aunt
records.form_basis: "not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister" (18:13)

records.title: Do not have sexual relations with your paternal uncle's wife
records.form_basis: "you shall not go in to his wife" (18:14)

records.title: Do not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law
records.form_basis: "You shall not uncover your daughter-in-law’s nakedness" (18:15)

records.title: Do not have sexual relations with your brother's wife, subject to the separately stated levirate provision
records.form_basis: "not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife" (18:16)

records.title: Do not take a woman together with her daughter or granddaughter for sexual relations
records.form_basis: "shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman" (18:17)

records.title: Do not take a wife's sister as a rival during your wife's lifetime
records.form_basis: "shall not take a woman … as a rival" (18:18)

records.title: Do not have sexual relations during menstrual separation
records.form_basis: "you shall not approach a woman in separation" (18:19)
records.note: Defined by menstrual impurity, so Ritual purity; but it stands among Lev 18's sexual prohibitions (cf. Ezek 18:6), so Moral secondary. Aquinas calls it both ceremonial and moral.

records.title: Do not give your offspring to serve a ruler in the stated cultic practice
records.form_basis: "you shall not give any of your seed" (18:21)
records.note: The compiler replaced the Saints Translation word ‘seed’ with ‘613 match’ inside the biblical quotation.

records.title: Do not profane God's holy name
records.form_basis: "neither shall you profane the holy name" (18:21)
records.note: P9 (sanctify the Name) is the positive counterpart from 22:32; this verse states only the prohibition, so not mixed.

records.title: Do not have male-male intercourse as with a woman
records.form_basis: "you shall not lie with a male" (18:22)

records.title: Do not have sexual relations with an animal
records.form_basis: "you shall not lie with any four-footed animal" (18:23)

records.title: Native and resident foreigner must avoid the prohibited acts under the stated covenant penalty
records.form_basis: "do none of these abominations" (18:26)
records.note: 'Keep My statutes' (18:26, 30) is a general exhortation framing the ban, not a separate requirement; the penalty is divine cutting-off, not a court penalty.

records.title: Revere father and mother
records.form_basis: "Each shall revere his father and his mother" (19:3)

records.title: Do not turn toward idols
records.form_basis: "You shall not follow idols" (19:4)

records.title: Do not reap your field completely
records.form_basis: "you shall not wholly reap the harvest" (19:9)
records.note: P120's duty to leave the corner is stated in 19:10 (record C0601); 19:9 itself only forbids, so not mixed.

records.title: Do not collect the harvest gleanings
records.form_basis: "shall not gather what falls from your harvest" (19:9)
records.note: P121's duty to leave the gleanings is stated in 19:10 (record C0601); 19:9 itself only forbids, so not mixed.

records.title: Do not strip the vineyard by a second gleaning
records.form_basis: "neither shall you glean your vineyard again" (19:10)
records.note: The regleaning ban is this record's provision. C0601 independently records the positive duty to leave the produce. Use the same separate-clause treatment as C0597 and C0598.

records.title: Do not gather the vineyard's fallen grapes
records.form_basis: "nor gather the grapes of your vineyard" (19:10)
records.note: The grape-gathering ban is this record's provision. C0601 independently records the positive duty to leave the produce. Use the same separate-clause treatment as C0597 and C0598.

records.title: Leave the prescribed harvest portions for the poor and resident foreigner
records.form_basis: "you shall leave them for the poor" (19:10)
records.note: This record covers the duty to leave produce for the poor and resident foreigner. The negative provisions are separately indexed as C0597–C0600.

records.title: Do not lie
records.form_basis: "You shall not lie" (19:11)

records.title: Do not defraud your neighbour
records.form_basis: "No one shall defraud his neighbour" (19:11)

records.title: Do not swear falsely by God's name
records.form_basis: "you shall not swear by My name" (19:12)

records.title: Do not wrong your neighbour
records.form_basis: "You shall not wrong your neighbour" (19:13)

records.title: Do not rob your neighbour
records.form_basis: "neither shall you rob" (19:13)

records.title: Do not withhold the hired worker's wages beyond the prescribed time
records.form_basis: "shall in no wise remain with you overnight" (19:13)
records.note: The exact overnight payroll deadline addresses an employer as such, fitting Civil as primary and Moral as secondary. The current order reflects the broader moral duty against withholding wages.

records.title: Do not curse the deaf
records.form_basis: "You shall not speak evil of the deaf" (19:14)

records.title: Do not put an obstacle before the blind
records.form_basis: "neither shall you put a stumbling block" (19:14)

records.title: Do not favour the powerful in judgment
records.form_basis: "neither shall you admire … the mighty" (19:15)
records.note: Impartiality is a moral duty; it is addressed to those judging, so the court setting gives Civil secondary.

records.title: Judge your neighbour righteously
records.form_basis: "you shall judge your neighbour in righteousness" (19:15)
records.note: Mixed: the verse also forbids 'injustice in judgment' (N273). Just judgment as a moral duty; Civil secondary for the court setting.

records.title: Do not go about deceitfully among your people
records.form_basis: "You shall not go about deceitfully" (19:16)

records.title: Do not conspire against your neighbour's life
records.form_basis: "you shall not conspire against the blood" (19:16)

records.title: Do not hate your brother inwardly
records.form_basis: "You shall not hate your brother" (19:17)

records.title: Reprove your neighbour
records.form_basis: "you shall surely reprove your neighbour" (19:17)

records.title: Do not bear sin because of your neighbour
records.form_basis: "you shall not bear sin because of him" (19:17)

records.title: Do not take vengeance
records.form_basis: "your hand shall not take vengeance" (19:18)

records.title: Do not hold a grudge
records.form_basis: "neither shall you remain angry" (19:18)

records.title: Do not mate livestock of different kinds
records.form_basis: "you shall not mate your livestock" (19:19)

records.title: Do not sow mixed kinds in the cultivated plot
records.form_basis: "neither shall you sow your vineyard" (19:19)

records.title: Do not wear the prohibited mixed-material garment
records.form_basis: "nor put upon yourself a spurious garment" (19:19)

records.title: Apply the prescribed inquiry rather than death in the case of the unfreed betrothed slave woman
records.form_basis: court procedure: "there shall be an inquiry concerning them" (19:20)
records.note: 'They shall not die' limits the penalty within the same court rule rather than adding a separate prohibition; Moral secondary because the underlying act is a sexual wrong.

records.title: Bring the guilt ram for intercourse with the unfreed betrothed slave woman
records.form_basis: "he shall bring his guilt offering" (19:21)

records.title: Do not eat a newly planted fruit tree's produce during its first three years
records.form_basis: "it shall not be eaten" (19:23)
records.note: 'You shall purge its uncleanness' declares the fruit's restricted status; the operative rule is the eating ban, so not treated as mixed.

records.title: Consecrate the fourth-year fruit to God
records.form_basis: status rule: "all its fruit shall be holy" (19:24)
records.note: Holy fourth-year fruit given in praise to the Lord, like firstfruits; it could also sit under Dietary laws (young trees) or consecrated items.

records.title: Fruit of the newly planted tree may be eaten from its fifth year
records.form_basis: "in the fifth year you shall eat" (19:25)
records.note: 'You shall eat' releases the fruit for use ('an increase unto you') after the restricted years; it imposes no duty to eat, so Permission.

records.title: Do not eat on the mountains, as the Saints text states
records.form_basis: "You shall not eat on the mountains" (19:26)
records.note: The Saints mountain wording can suggest a cultic meal, as in Ezekiel 18:6. Maimonides derives the rebellious son's gluttonous eating and drinking prohibition from the Hebrew wording. His N195 is not a simple dietary blood ban.

records.title: Do not practice divination by omens
records.form_basis: "You shall not divine by omens" (19:26)

records.title: Do not practice bird-based augury
records.form_basis: "You shall not … observe birds for divination" (19:26)

records.title: Do not make the prohibited haircut called sisoe in the Saints text
records.form_basis: "You shall not make a sisoe" (19:27)
records.note: A bodily holiness marker separating Israel from gentile practice; filed under Signs, vows and dedications as the nearest area.

records.title: Do not mar the prescribed appearance of the beard
records.form_basis: "shall not … spoil the appearance of your beards" (19:27)
records.note: Bodily holiness marker like the sisoe ban; Signs, vows and dedications is the nearest area.

records.title: Do not perform the prohibited bodily mourning rites for the dead
records.form_basis: "you shall make no incisions in your body" (19:28)
records.note: Pagan mourning rite banned as a holiness marker; read as a pagan-worship ban it would be Moral. Signs, vows and dedications is the nearest area.

records.title: Do not put tattooed inscriptions on your body
records.form_basis: "neither shall you put tattooed letters upon yourselves" (19:28)
records.note: Bodily marking banned beside the mourning cuts as a holiness marker; some read it as a moral ban on pagan marks. Signs, vows and dedications is the nearest area.

records.title: Do not make your daughter a prostitute
records.form_basis: "You shall not profane your daughter" (19:29)

records.title: Revere the Lord’s holy things
records.form_basis: "revere My holy things" (19:30)

records.title: Do not consult spirit mediums
records.form_basis: "You shall not follow spirit mediums" (19:31)

records.title: Do not turn to enchanters
records.form_basis: "neither shall you attach yourselves unto enchanters" (19:31)

records.title: Rise before the grey-haired and honour the elder
records.form_basis: "rise before the face of the grey-haired" (19:32)

records.title: Use just scales, weights and measures
records.form_basis: "You shall have just scales, just weights" (19:36)
records.note: Also holds the prohibition 'You shall do no injustice in … measures, weights, or scales' (19:35).

records.title: Execute by stoning the person giving offspring to the prohibited cultic service
records.form_basis: court penalty: "the nation upon the land shall stone him" (20:2)

records.title: Do not overlook the prohibited offering of offspring
records.form_basis: "utterly overlook that man with their eyes" (20:4)
records.note: Leviticus 20:5 announces divine judgment on the offender, his household and those joining the practice. It does not specify punishment for merely overlooking him. The enforcement duty appears in 20:2.

records.title: Apply the prescribed death judgment to the adulterer and adulteress
records.form_basis: court penalty: "shall surely be put to death" (20:10)

records.title: Apply the prescribed death judgment for intercourse with the father's wife
records.form_basis: court penalty: "Both shall surely be put to death" (20:11)

records.title: Apply the prescribed death judgment for intercourse with the daughter-in-law
records.form_basis: court penalty: "both shall surely be put to death" (20:12)

records.title: Apply the prescribed death judgment for male-male intercourse
records.form_basis: court penalty: "They shall be put to death" (20:13)

records.title: Apply the prescribed burning judgment for taking a woman and her mother
records.form_basis: court penalty: "They shall burn him and them with fire" (20:14)

records.title: Kill the animal involved in the prohibited sexual act
records.form_basis: court penalty: "you shall kill the animal" (20:15)

records.title: Apply the prescribed stoning judgment to the spirit-medium or enchanter
records.form_basis: court penalty: "You shall stone them with stones" (20:27)

records.title: Ordinary priests: avoid corpse defilement except for the specified close relatives
records.form_basis: "They shall not be defiled for dead persons" (21:1)
records.note: The Saints wording expressly permits corpse defilement for named relatives. The record is the prohibition with an exception. Maimonides P37 derives a duty of mourning from the Hebrew verse and is a distinct interpretive point.

records.title: Do not shave a mourning bald patch
records.form_basis: "you shall not shave a bald patch" (21:5)

records.title: Priests: be holy to God and do not profane his name
records.form_basis: "They shall be holy to their God" (21:6)
records.note: Maimonides explicitly cites Leviticus 21:6 for N76, so saying it does not fit the verse is misleading. He derives a narrower sanctuary-service ban from it. The Saints record's general holiness duty and profanation ban still justify Positive and mixed.

records.title: Priests: do not marry a prostitute
records.form_basis: "not take a woman who is a prostitute" (21:7)

records.title: Priests: do not marry a profaned woman
records.form_basis: "shall not take a woman who is … profaned" (21:7)

records.title: Priests: do not marry a divorced woman
records.form_basis: "not take … a woman expelled by her husband" (21:7)

records.title: Regard and maintain the priest's consecrated status
records.form_basis: "he shall sanctify him" (21:8)

records.title: Apply the prescribed burning judgment to a priest's daughter who prostitutes herself
records.form_basis: court penalty: "She shall be burned with fire" (21:9)
records.note: Penalty is Civil; the act is sexual immorality (Moral), aggravated by the priestly status.

records.title: High priest: do not remove your turban
records.form_basis: "shall not remove his turban" (21:10)

records.title: High priest: do not tear your garments in mourning
records.form_basis: "neither shall he rend his garments" (21:10)

records.title: High priest: do not incur corpse defilement, even for parents
records.form_basis: "he shall not make himself unclean" (21:11)

records.title: High priest: do not leave the sanctuary service for mourning
records.form_basis: "he shall not leave the holy precincts" (21:12)

records.title: High priest: do not profane your consecrated ministry
records.form_basis: "shall not … profane what is consecrated" (21:12)

records.title: High priest: marry a virgin from your own kin
records.form_basis: "He shall take a virgin wife" (21:13)
records.note: The prohibition in 21:14 is recorded separately (C0667).

records.title: High priest: do not marry a widow, an expelled or profaned woman, or a prostitute
records.form_basis: "these he shall not take" (21:14)
records.note: The positive duty to marry a virgin is recorded separately (C0666).

records.title: High priest: do not profane your offspring through the forbidden marriage
records.form_basis: "shall not profane his seed among his people" (21:15)
records.note: The compiler replaced the Saints Translation word ‘seed’ with ‘613 match’ inside the biblical quotation.

records.title: A priest with a specified blemish: do not approach to offer at the altar or enter beyond the permitted boundary
records.form_basis: "shall not draw near to present the gifts" (21:17)
records.note: The 21:22 permission to eat holy portions is recorded separately (TL-03-21-22).

records.title: A priest with a specified blemish may eat the holy and most holy portions
records.form_basis: "He may eat the gifts of God" (21:22)

records.title: Priests: do not approach or eat holy things while unclean
records.form_basis: "shall not eat the holy things" (22:4)

records.title: Priests: avoid the uncleanness of eating an animal found dead or torn by beasts
records.form_basis: "He shall not eat an animal found dead" (22:8)

records.title: A priest's lodger or hired worker may not eat holy things
records.form_basis: "lodger or hired worker shall not eat" (22:10)

records.title: A priest's purchased or house-born slaves may eat his holy food
records.form_basis: "he may eat of his bread" (22:11)

records.title: A priest's daughter married to an outsider may not eat holy portions
records.form_basis: "she shall not eat the first portions" (22:12)

records.title: A returning childless priest's daughter may again eat her father's food
records.form_basis: "may eat her father’s bread" (22:13)
records.note: The closing 'no outsider shall eat of it' restates the ban at AUD-03-22-10.

records.title: Repay holy food eaten in ignorance with an added fifth
records.form_basis: restitution: "he shall add a fifth to it" (22:14)
records.note: Restitution to the priest for sacred food: the holy portion makes it chiefly Ceremonial, with restitution as a Civil second character.

records.title: Do not profane Israel's holy contributions
records.form_basis: "they shall not profane the holy things" (22:15)
records.note: 613 match N153 (untithed produce) is a rabbinic derivation; the verse itself bars priests from profaning Israel's holy contributions.

records.title: Do not offer blemished or mutilated animals, including those supplied by foreigners
records.form_basis: "They shall not bring anything with a blemish" (22:20)
records.note: Also holds the requirement 'it shall be unblemished to be accepted' (22:21; P61). The 22:23 permission and castration ban are recorded separately.

records.title: The specified calf or sheep with a cut ear or shortened tail may be slaughtered for personal use
records.form_basis: "you may slaughter for yourself a calf" (22:23)
records.note: The verse's vow restriction ('it shall not be accepted') belongs with C0675.

records.title: Do not perform the prohibited animal castration
records.form_basis: "in your land you shall not do this" (22:24)
records.note: Grows out of the altar rule on mutilated animals, so read as a Ceremonial holiness rule, though 'in your land' extends it to husbandry generally.

records.title: A calf, sheep or goat becomes eligible for offering from its eighth day
records.form_basis: status rule: "shall remain under its mother for seven days" (22:27)
records.note: 'May be accepted' sounds permissive, but the rule fixes a status (seven days under the mother first), matching 613 match P60, so Positive.

records.title: Do not slaughter a mother animal and its young on the same day
records.form_basis: "shall not slaughter … together with her young" (22:28)
records.note: The verse gives a same-day slaughter ban without limiting it to offerings. Maimonides N101 covers ordinary and consecrated animals. Ceremonial fits the surrounding passage, with an alternative Civil reading for livestock practice.

records.title: Present the peace or thanksgiving sacrifice according to its acceptance requirements
records.form_basis: "shall sacrifice it so that it is acceptable" (22:29)

records.title: Hold a holy Sabbath assembly
records.form_basis: "a holy convocation unto the Lord" (23:3)
records.note: The record is specifically the Sabbath convocation, a festival observance. The neighboring work ban belongs to Sabbath rest, so it does not make the assembly mixed or bring it under the Ten Commandments tie-breaker.

records.title: Present the prescribed seven days of Unleavened Bread offerings
records.form_basis: "you shall bring whole burnt offerings" (23:8)
records.note: The verse's seventh-day convocation and no-work clause are separate festival-day rules.

records.title: Offer the prescribed lamb, grain, oil and wine with the first sheaf
records.form_basis: "you shall offer an unblemished year-old sheep" (23:12)

records.title: Do not eat the new grain before bringing the appointed offering
records.form_basis: "shall eat neither bread nor roasted fresh grain" (23:14)
records.note: Treated as a food prohibition (Dietary laws), though it is tied to the sheaf offering.

records.title: Count the seven complete weeks and fifty days to the new grain offering
records.form_basis: "you shall count … seven complete weeks" (23:15)

records.title: Bring the two prescribed Weeks firstfruits loaves
records.form_basis: "you shall bring bread as a presentation" (23:17)

records.title: Offer the prescribed burnt, sin and peace offerings with the Weeks loaves
records.form_basis: "with the loaves you shall bring" (23:18)

records.title: Give the consecrated Weeks presentation to the officiating priest
records.form_basis: "they shall belong unto the priest" (23:20)

records.title: Hold a holy assembly at Weeks
records.form_basis: "you shall proclaim this day a convocation" (23:21)
records.note: The verse's no-work clause is recorded separately (C0690).

records.title: Do no prohibited work at Weeks
records.form_basis: "You shall do no laborious work on it" (23:21)
records.note: The record is the Weeks work prohibition. The positive convocation is C0689. P162's positive phrasing of rest does not add a separate affirmative clause to this specific Saints provision.

records.title: Keep the first day of the seventh month as a trumpet memorial
records.form_basis: "shall have a rest, a memorial of trumpets" (23:24)

records.title: Hold its holy assembly
records.form_basis: "it shall be a holy convocation for you" (23:24)

records.title: Do no prohibited work on the trumpet memorial
records.form_basis: "You shall do no laborious work" (23:25)
records.note: The trumpet memorial work prohibition has no affirmative rest clause in 23:25. The affirmative observance is C0691 (23:24) and the offering in 23:25 is C0694. P163 is a traditional positive counterpart.

records.title: Bring the prescribed trumpet-memorial offering
records.form_basis: "you shall bring a whole burnt offering" (23:25)
records.note: The verse's no-work clause is recorded separately (C0693).

records.title: Hold a holy assembly on the Day of Atonement
records.form_basis: "it shall be a holy convocation unto you" (23:27)

records.title: Bring the prescribed Day of Atonement offering
records.form_basis: "bring a whole burnt offering unto the Lord" (23:27)

records.title: Hold the holy assemblies on the first and eighth days of Booths
records.form_basis: "there shall be a holy convocation" (23:35)
records.note: The no-work clauses are recorded separately (C0698).

records.title: Do no prohibited work on the first and eighth days of Booths
records.form_basis: "You shall do no laborious work" (23:35)
records.note: The two Booths work bans are the indexed provisions. The positive assemblies and offerings in these verses have separate records C0697, C0699, and C0700. P166/P167 do not supply additional operative clauses in this record.

records.title: Bring the prescribed daily Booths offerings
records.form_basis: "seven days you shall bring whole burnt offerings" (23:36)

records.title: Bring the prescribed eighth-day closing offering
records.form_basis: "eighth day … you shall bring whole burnt offerings" (23:36)

records.title: Present the festival offerings in addition to the regular, vowed and freewill offerings
records.form_basis: "to present offerings unto the Lord" (23:37)

records.title: Take the prescribed branches and fruit for Booths
records.form_basis: "on the first day you shall take" (23:40)

records.title: Native Israelites: dwell in booths for the appointed seven days
records.form_basis: "You shall dwell in tents seven days" (23:42)

records.title: Aaron and sons: eat the bread of the Presence in a holy place
records.form_basis: "shall eat these things in a holy place" (24:9)

records.title: Apply the prescribed stoning judgment for the blasphemy described in the text
records.form_basis: court penalty: "Let the whole congregation of Israel stone him" (24:16)
records.note: 613 match N60 is the underlying blasphemy ban; this record is the court's stoning penalty, which Maimonides counts among positive commandments.

records.title: Do not curse God
records.form_basis: "A man who curses God shall bear sin" (24:15)
records.note: Casuistic 'shall bear sin' states the ban; the death penalty is recorded at C0709.

records.title: Compensate for killing another person's animal
records.form_basis: restitution: "shall repay life for life" (24:18)

records.title: Apply one judgment to native Israelites and resident foreigners in the stated cases
records.form_basis: "There shall be one judgment" (24:22)
records.note: A rule for Israel's courts (one law for native and foreigner), not a worship rite, so Civil; impartial justice gives a Moral second character.

records.title: Do not sow fields in the sabbatical year
records.form_basis: "You shall not sow your field" (25:4)

records.title: Do not prune vines in the sabbatical year
records.form_basis: "You shall not … prune your vine" (25:4)

records.title: Do not reap volunteer crops as an ordinary harvest in the sabbatical year
records.form_basis: "shall not reap the things growing of themselves" (25:5)

records.title: Do not gather the unpruned vine's produce as an ordinary harvest in the sabbatical year
records.form_basis: "shall not … gather the grapes of your consecration" (25:5)

records.title: Proclaim Jubilee release throughout the land with the appointed trumpet
records.form_basis: "you shall make proclamation with a trumpet" (25:9)

records.title: Consecrate the fiftieth year
records.form_basis: "you shall consecrate the fiftieth year" (25:10)
records.note: The discrete provision consecrates the fiftieth year as sacred, favoring Ceremonial primary. The repository's Jubilee tie-breaker favors the existing Civil primary, so the category order depends on how the convention is applied.

records.title: Restore ancestral landholdings at the Jubilee
records.form_basis: "each one shall depart unto his possession" (25:10)

records.title: Do not sow in the Jubilee year
records.form_basis: "You shall not sow" (25:11)

records.title: Do not reap volunteer crops as an ordinary harvest in the Jubilee year
records.form_basis: "You shall not … reap what grows of itself" (25:11)

records.title: Do not gather the unpruned vine's produce as an ordinary harvest in the Jubilee year
records.form_basis: "shall not … gather its consecrated produce" (25:11)

records.title: Use the Jubilee produce as the prescribed field food
records.form_basis: "You shall eat its produce from the fields" (25:12)
records.note: 'You shall eat … from the fields' could be read as permission to eat the untended yield; taken here as prescribing how Jubilee produce is eaten.

records.title: Do not wrong your neighbour when buying or selling
records.form_basis: "let no man oppress his neighbour" (25:14)
records.note: 613 match P245 rests on the conditional 'if one sells' (sale law), not a stated duty, so not mixed.

records.title: Price land transfers according to the remaining harvest years before Jubilee
records.form_basis: "you shall increase its purchase price" (25:16)

records.title: Do not oppress one another, but fear your God
records.form_basis: "Let no man oppress his neighbour" (25:17)
records.note: Also holds the positive 'you shall fear the Lord your God' (25:17).

records.title: Do not sell the land permanently
records.form_basis: "the land shall not be sold in perpetuity" (25:23)

records.title: Permit and calculate redemption of ancestral land according to the prescribed rules
records.form_basis: "you shall provide redemption for the land" (25:24)
records.note: Title says 'permit', but 25:24 requires granting redemption, and the kinsman 'shall redeem' (25:25).

records.title: Apply the stated redemption periods and Jubilee distinctions for walled-city and village houses
records.form_basis: status rule: "its redemption shall be possible until a year" (25:29)

records.title: Preserve the Levites' continuing house-redemption and Jubilee rights
records.form_basis: status rule: "shall always be redeemable by the Levites" (25:32)

records.title: Do not sell the Levite cities' pasture land
records.form_basis: "the fields … shall not be sold" (25:34)

records.title: Do not impose ordinary slave service on an impoverished Israelite brother
records.form_basis: "shall not serve … service of a household slave" (25:39)
records.note: Also holds the requirement 'He shall be with you as a hired worker' (25:40).

records.title: Release the Israelite bondservant and children at Jubilee
records.form_basis: "he shall go out at the release" (25:41)

records.title: Do not sell an Israelite brother in the manner of a slave sale
records.form_basis: "one shall not be sold with the sale" (25:42)

records.title: Do not rule over the Israelite servant ruthlessly
records.form_basis: "You shall not wear him down with toil" (25:43)
records.note: The record forbids wearing down an Israelite servant with toil. The adjacent call to fear God supplies a religious motive outside the specific rule. Compare AUD-03-25-17, whose title deliberately includes both commands.

records.title: Apply the ancient rules for acquiring and inheriting enslaved foreigners
records.form_basis: "they shall be held by you permanently" (25:46)
records.note: Acquisition is permissive ('you may acquire', 25:44); the inheritance and permanent-holding rule (613 match P235) is the status to apply. The closing ban on harsh toil protects Israelites, a separate provision.

records.title: Permit redemption of an Israelite sold to a foreigner and calculate it by years remaining
records.form_basis: status rule: "he shall have a right of redemption" (25:48)
records.note: The named provision establishes a legal right and requires a calculation if exercised. The relatives' choice to redeem is permissive, but it does not make the legally required procedure discretionary. Compare C0727 and C0728.

records.title: Do not let a foreign owner work an Israelite harshly
records.form_basis: "you shall not wear him down with toil" (25:53)
records.note: Servant law the community must enforce ('before you'), so Civil; the ban on harsh treatment is also a moral duty against oppression, hence Moral secondary.

records.title: Release the unredeemed Israelite and his children at Jubilee when held by a resident foreigner
records.form_basis: release rule: "shall go out in the year of release" (25:54)
records.note: Release of a bonded Israelite at the year of release is servant and economic law (Civil); it does not concern the Jubilee's sacred proclamation, so no Ceremonial secondary.

records.title: Do not erect an idolatrous pillar
records.form_basis: "nor shall you set up a pillar" (26:1)

records.title: Do not place a figured stone for worship
records.form_basis: "You shall not ... place a conspicuous stone" (26:1)

records.title: Apply the prescribed person-vow valuations, including the poor person's assessment
records.form_basis: valuation rule: "the valuation of a male ... shall be fifty" (27:3)

records.title: Do not exchange a consecrated sacrificial animal
records.form_basis: "He shall not exchange it" (27:10)
records.note: Area: a vowed animal given to the Lord is a consecrated item; Sacrifice and offerings is also possible.

records.title: Treat both original and substituted sacrificial animals as holy
records.form_basis: status rule: "both it and its substitute shall be holy" (27:10)
records.note: Area as C0741: the vowed animal and its substitute are consecrated items; Sacrifice and offerings is also possible.

records.title: Treat the priest’s valuation of the specified vowed livestock or consecrated house as binding
records.form_basis: valuation rule: "As the priest values it ... shall stand" (27:12)

records.title: Add a fifth when redeeming the vowed animal
records.form_basis: "he shall add a fifth to its valuation" (27:13)

records.title: Add a fifth when redeeming the consecrated house
records.form_basis: "he shall add a fifth of the silver" (27:15)

records.title: Value a consecrated ancestral field by its seed and remaining Jubilee years
records.form_basis: valuation rule: "the valuation shall be according to its seed" (27:16)
records.note: The compiler replaced the Saints Translation word ‘seed’ with ‘613 match’ inside the biblical quotation.

records.title: Add a fifth when redeeming the consecrated ancestral field
records.form_basis: "he shall add a fifth of the silver" (27:19)

records.title: Do not redeem the consecrated field after the stated disqualifying sale
records.form_basis: "he shall no longer redeem it" (27:20)
records.note: Could be read as a status rule (the redemption right lapses), but the operative words forbid further redemption, matching the title, so Negative.

records.title: Assign the unredeemed consecrated field to the priest at Jubilee
records.form_basis: status rule: "It shall become the priest’s possession" (27:21)

records.title: Assess and pay the prescribed value for a consecrated purchased field
records.form_basis: "he shall repay the valuation on that day" (27:23)

records.title: Return a consecrated purchased field to its original owner at Jubilee
records.form_basis: status rule: "the field shall be returned to the man" (27:24)
records.note: Jubilee reversion of land to its ancestral holder is land-tenure law (Civil); it applies to a field consecrated by its buyer, so Ceremonial secondary (dedications).

records.title: Use the prescribed sanctuary weight for valuations
records.form_basis: "every valuation shall be by sacred weights" (27:25)

records.title: Do not vow as a new dedication a firstborn animal already belonging to God
records.form_basis: "none shall consecrate it" (27:26)
