records.note: Area: the forbidden act is consecrating (vowing) a firstborn, so Signs, vows and dedications rather than Sacrifice and offerings.

records.title: Redeem the unclean firstborn at its assessed value plus a fifth, or sell it at the valuation
records.form_basis: "he shall exchange it according to its valuation" (27:27)

records.title: Do not sell an irrevocably devoted thing
records.form_basis: "he shall neither sell nor redeem" (27:28)

records.title: Do not redeem an irrevocably devoted thing
records.form_basis: "he shall neither sell nor redeem" (27:28)

records.title: Do not ransom a person placed under the stated death devotion
records.form_basis: "shall not be redeemed" (27:29)
records.note: A person 'devoted' must die: read as penal law (Civil, matching the site label); the devoted-things institution gives the Ceremonial secondary. Could be read as Ceremonial primary.

records.title: Carry out the stated death devotion
records.form_basis: death consequence: "but shall surely be put to death" (27:29)
records.note: Leviticus 27:29 states a death consequence for devotion and names no court or trial. The broader category remains borderline because the provision sits among laws of consecration.

records.title: Set apart the prescribed tithe of produce and livestock as holy to God
records.form_basis: "the tenth shall be holy unto the Lord" (27:32)

records.title: Add a fifth when redeeming the produce tithe
records.form_basis: "he shall add a fifth part unto it" (27:31)
records.note: Area follows the tithe (Sacrifice and offerings); the redemption-plus-a-fifth pattern also fits Signs, vows and dedications.

records.title: Do not exchange the tithe animal
records.form_basis: "You shall not exchange a good one" (27:33)
records.note: Area: a tithe animal, so Sacrifice and offerings (tithes).

records.title: Treat a substituted tithe animal as holy alongside the original
records.form_basis: status rule: "its substitute also shall be holy" (27:33)

records.title: Do not redeem the tithe animal or its substitute
records.form_basis: "it shall not be redeemed" (27:33)

records.title: Levites: carry the tabernacle and its furnishings in their assigned service
records.form_basis: "They shall carry the Tent" (1:50)

records.title: Apply the stated death liability to unauthorized sanctuary intrusion
records.form_basis: death liability: "Let an outsider who approaches die" (1:51)
records.note: Numbers 1:51 and the related sanctuary passages state death liability for an outsider who approaches. They name no court or executor. Retain Positive for the stated status and use Ceremonial for sanctuary access.

records.title: Levites: guard the tabernacle and its furnishings
records.form_basis: "the Levites themselves shall keep the charge" (1:53)
records.note: 613 match N67 (do not leave it unguarded) is implied by the guard duty, but the verse states no prohibition, so not mixed.

records.title: Aaron and sons: keep the priestly charge of altar and inner sanctuary
records.form_basis: "they shall keep their priesthood" (3:10)
records.note: 613 match N67 (do not leave the sanctuary unguarded) is the negative side of this charge; the verse's operative words are positive ('they shall keep their priesthood').

records.title: The Levites belong to the Lord in place of Israel’s firstborn
records.form_basis: status rule: "the Levites shall be Mine" (3:12)
records.note: A divine declaration, not a command; read as a status rule (Positive). Area could also be Signs, vows and dedications (the Levites as ransom for the firstborn).

records.title: Kohathites: do not touch the holy things themselves when carrying them
records.form_basis: "they shall not touch the holy things" (4:15)

records.title: Kohathites: do not go in suddenly to look upon the holy things
records.form_basis: "they shall in no wise enter to behold" (4:20)

records.title: Exclude persons with the specified impurity from Israel’s sanctuary camp
records.form_basis: "send them outside the camp" (5:3)
records.note: Also holds the prohibition 'they shall in no wise defile their camps' (5:3), 613 match N77; the title's main clause is the duty to send them out.

records.title: Give the restitution to the priest when the injured person has no receiving kinsman
records.form_basis: status rule: "the repayment ... shall be the priest’s" (5:8)
records.note: Restitution law (Civil, matching the site label), but the payment goes to the priest as made 'unto the Lord', beside the ram of atonement, so Ceremonial secondary.

records.title: Give the prescribed firstfruits and sacred contributions to the priests
records.form_basis: "unto the priest, shall belong to him" (5:9)

records.title: Do not put oil or frankincense on the jealousy offering
records.form_basis: "He shall pour no oil upon it" (5:15)

records.title: Apply the stated jealousy law in the case it defines
records.form_basis: "the priest shall perform all this law" (5:30)
records.note: A priestly rite before the Lord (Ceremonial) that settles a husband's accusation with legal effect ('free from sin', 'bear her sin'), so Civil secondary.

records.title: Nazirite: abstain from wine and strong drink
records.form_basis: abstention: "wine and strong drink, he shall be purified" (6:3)
records.note: Numbers 6:3 addresses wine and strong drink directly. Verse 4 concerns vine products more broadly. The form remains Negative because the law requires abstention.

records.title: Nazirite: abstain from wine vinegar and fermented-drink vinegar
records.form_basis: "He shall drink neither vinegar of wine" (6:3)

records.title: Nazirite: abstain from grapes and other vine products
records.form_basis: "he shall eat neither fresh grapes nor raisins" (6:3)

records.title: Nazirite: let your hair grow and do not put a razor to it during the vow
records.form_basis: "letting the hair of his head grow long" (6:5)
records.note: Also holds the prohibition 'no razor shall come upon his head' (6:5), 613 match N209; the title leads with letting the hair grow.

records.title: Nazirite: do not incur corpse defilement, even for close relatives
records.form_basis: "he shall not defile himself when they die" (6:7)

records.title: Nazirite: restart the vow period after defilement
records.form_basis: status rule: "the former days shall not be reckoned" (6:12)
records.note: 'Shall not be reckoned' sets how the vow is counted (a status rule), not a ban; its effect is that the vow period restarts, so Positive.

records.title: A Nazirite may drink wine again after completing the prescribed rite
records.form_basis: "afterward he who has vowed shall drink wine" (6:20)
records.note: 'Shall drink wine' ends the abstention rather than imposing a duty; read as restored permission, per the title and context note.

records.title: Nazirites: bring the gift undertaken in the vow of consecration
records.form_basis: "according to the extent of his vow" (6:21)
records.note: The Saints text is a summary formula with no explicit 'shall'; the duty to bring the gift 'according to the extent of his vow' makes it Positive.

records.title: Aaron and sons: bless Israel with the appointed words and God's name
records.form_basis: "Thus you shall bless the sons of Israel" (6:23)

records.title: Observe the stated Levite entry, retirement and assistance ages
records.form_basis: "Thus you shall deal with the Levites" (8:26)
records.note: Also holds the prohibition that a retired Levite 'shall perform no work' (8:25–26), only assisting with the charges; the main clause sets the service ages.

records.title: Keep the second-month Passover when prevented by the specified uncleanness or journey
records.form_basis: "In the second month ... they shall observe it" (9:11)

records.title: Do not neglect the Passover when clean and not travelling
records.form_basis: penalty for omission: "fails to observe the Passover ... shall be destroyed" (9:13)
records.note: The title is worded negatively, but the verse penalises failing a positive duty ('fails to observe'), matching 613 match P55, so Positive.

records.title: Aaron's sons: sound the appointed trumpets
records.form_basis: "the priests, shall blow the trumpets" (10:8)
records.note: Area: 10:8 assigns the trumpet duty to the priests; Festivals and holy days is also possible.

records.title: Apply the same standing offering rule to native Israelites and resident sojourners
records.form_basis: "You shall have one law" (15:15)
records.note: Numbers 15:13–16 regulates offerings. Civil secondary captures the explicit parity for native and resident offerers, as with the Passover rule in Exodus 12:49.

records.title: Give the first portion of the dough to God
records.form_basis: "you shall set apart a loaf" (15:20)

records.title: Offer a year-old female goat for the individual inadvertent offense in this provision
records.form_basis: "he shall present one year-old female goat" (15:27)

records.title: Apply the stated judgment for defiant sin
records.form_basis: penalty: "that soul shall be destroyed from his people" (15:30)
records.note: Defiant contempt for God’s word is the stated offense. The passage gives a consequence without assigning enforcement to a court. Moral fits the offense, and Positive describes the sanction under the project’s status-rule convention.

records.title: Make the prescribed fringes at the corners of the garment
records.form_basis: "Let them make for themselves fringes" (15:38)

records.title: No non-Aaronide may approach to offer incense
records.form_basis: "no outsider ... should approach to place incense" (17:5)

records.title: Bear the assigned responsibility for sanctuary and priesthood
records.form_basis: "You and your sons ... shall bear the sins" (18:1)

records.title: Levites: do not usurp priestly access to the holy vessels and altar
records.form_basis: "they shall not approach the holy vessels" (18:3)

records.title: Israelites outside the appointed service: do not approach the restricted sanctuary ministry
records.form_basis: "the outsider shall not approach you" (18:4)

records.title: Aaron’s priestly house receives the prescribed holy contributions by everlasting ordinance
records.form_basis: grant: "I have given unto you ... an everlasting ordinance" (18:19)
records.note: A divine grant read as a status rule (the contributions are the priests' due); it could be read as Permission. Area: priests' portions as offerings.

records.title: The reserved portions of the most holy offerings are allotted to Aaron and his sons
records.form_basis: status rule: "it shall be yours and your sons" (18:9)

records.title: Priests' clean household members may eat the presented gifts
records.form_basis: "Everyone clean in your house shall eat them" (18:11)
records.note: 'Shall eat them' extends the right to eat to the clean household; read as permission, per the title.

records.title: Everything devoted in Israel belongs to the priests
records.form_basis: status rule: "Everything devoted ... shall be yours" (18:14)
records.note: Area: devoted things (Signs, vows and dedications); as a priests' portion it could be Sacrifice and offerings.

records.title: Redeem the firstborn of unclean livestock
records.form_basis: "you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean livestock" (18:15)

records.title: Do not redeem firstborn cattle, sheep or goats
records.form_basis: "you shall not redeem the firstborn of calves" (18:17)

records.title: Give the clean firstborn sacrificial meat to the priest
records.form_basis: status rule: "their flesh shall be yours" (18:18)

records.title: Do not assign Aaron's and Levi's tribe an ordinary territorial inheritance
records.form_basis: "You shall not inherit in their land" (18:20)
records.note: Land-inheritance rule (Civil, matching the site label), grounded in the priestly tribe's status ('I am your portion'), so Ceremonial secondary.

records.title: Give Israel's service tithe to the Levites
records.form_basis: allotment: "I have given every tithe in Israel" (18:21)

records.title: Levites: set apart a tithe of the received tithe for the priest
records.form_basis: "you shall take ... a tithe of the tithe" (18:26)

records.title: Levites and their households may eat their remaining tithe anywhere after setting aside its consecrated portion
records.form_basis: "you shall eat it in every place" (18:31)
records.note: The operative clause allows Levites and their households to eat the remainder anywhere. The tithe duty is separately catalogued at C0883, and verse 32’s prohibition on profanation does not change the form of this permission.

records.title: Use an unblemished red heifer that has never borne a yoke
records.form_basis: "let them bring unto you a red heifer" (19:2)

records.title: The officiating priest and burner: remain unclean until evening
records.form_basis: impurity rule: "the priest shall be unclean until evening" (19:7)

records.title: The ash gatherer: wash garments and remain unclean until evening
records.form_basis: "shall wash his clothes and be unclean" (19:10)

records.title: Observe seven-day uncleanness after the specified human corpse, bone, grave or death-house contact
records.form_basis: impurity rule: "shall be unclean for seven days" (19:11)

records.title: Do not defile the Lord's tent by neglecting corpse purification
records.form_basis: implied ban: "has defiled the Tent ... shall be wiped out" (19:13)
records.note: No explicit 'do not': the cutting-off penalty for defiling the Tent while unpurified implies the prohibition (613 match N77). It also implies the duty to be purified.

records.title: Treat the uncovered open vessel in the death-house as unclean
records.form_basis: impurity rule: "every open vessel ... is unclean" (19:15)

records.title: Observe uncleanness until evening after the prescribed bathing
records.form_basis: impurity rule: "he shall be unclean until evening" (19:19)

records.title: The person touching purification water: remain unclean until evening
records.form_basis: impurity rule: "touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean" (19:21)

records.title: Apply the prescribed secondary-contact uncleanness rule
records.form_basis: impurity rule: "whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean" (19:22)

records.title: Phinehas and his descendants hold the covenant of priesthood
records.form_basis: status grant: "for him and his seed … covenant of priesthood" (25:13)
records.note: Restored the Saints Translation word “seed” in the priesthood covenant quotation. The compiler had replaced it with “613 match”.

records.title: Assign inheritance by the prescribed order of descendants and nearest kin
records.form_basis: "you shall assign his inheritance unto his daughter" (27:8)

records.title: Present God's prescribed offerings at their appointed times
records.form_basis: "You shall take care to present My gifts" (28:2)

records.title: Offer the additional Sabbath lambs with the prescribed accompaniments
records.form_basis: "on the Sabbath day you shall bring" (28:9)
records.note: Area could also be Festivals and holy days; the provision prescribes the offering itself.

records.title: Offer the prescribed new-moon burnt and sin offerings with their accompaniments
records.form_basis: "at the new moons you shall bring" (28:11)
records.note: Area could also be Festivals and holy days; the provision prescribes the offerings themselves.

records.title: Offer the prescribed Weeks burnt and sin offerings with their accompaniments
records.form_basis: "you shall bring whole burnt offerings" (28:27)
records.note: Area could also be Festivals and holy days; the provision prescribes the offerings themselves.

records.title: Do not profane or break your pledged word
records.form_basis: "shall not profane his word" (30:3)
records.note: Also requires 'He shall do everything that comes from his mouth' (613 match P94). Keeping oaths and vows to God is moral (no false oaths); the vow system is Ceremonial.

records.title: Apply the stated confirmation or timely annulment rules to a young daughter's vow
records.form_basis: status rule: "then all her vows shall stand" (30:5)
records.note: The father's legal authority over a dependant's vow is household law (Civil, matching the site label); the vows themselves are Ceremonial (Signs, vows and dedications). Could be Ceremonial primary.

records.title: Apply the stated confirmation, annulment and liability rules to a wife’s vow
records.form_basis: status rule: "then all her vows shall stand" (30:8)
records.note: The husband's legal authority over his wife's vow is marriage law (Civil, matching the site label); the vows themselves are Ceremonial. Could be Ceremonial primary.

records.title: Treat a widow's or divorced woman's vow as binding
records.form_basis: status: "shall remain against her" (30:10)
records.note: Vow law is Ceremonial per the brief; the site's civil label fits the legal-status side (no father or husband can annul her vow), so Civil is secondary.

records.title: Apply the prescribed purity standard to articles that can or cannot pass through fire
records.form_basis: "you shall thoroughly purify every covering" (31:20)

records.title: Give the Levites the prescribed towns and surrounding lands in proportion to tribal holdings
records.form_basis: "give the Levites towns to live in" (35:2)
records.note: Land allotment and measurement (Civil) for the landless Levites; their sacred status gives a Ceremonial secondary.

records.title: Set apart the appointed cities of refuge
records.form_basis: "you shall set apart towns for yourselves" (35:11)

records.title: Do not execute the manslayer before congregational judgment
records.form_basis: "the killer shall in no wise die before" (35:12)

records.title: Put to death whoever kills with a deadly weapon or in enmity
records.form_basis: court penalty: "Let the murderer surely be put to death" (35:16)

records.title: The blood-avenger: execute the condemned murderer under the prescribed judgment
records.form_basis: penalty: "shall himself kill the murderer" (35:19)

records.title: Judge intent and circumstances to distinguish murder from accidental killing
records.form_basis: "the congregation shall judge between the one" (35:24)

records.title: Congregation: rescue the accidental killer from the avenger of blood
records.form_basis: "the congregation shall rescue the killer" (35:25)

records.title: Remain in the city of refuge until the high priest dies
records.form_basis: "he must live in the city of refuge" (35:28)
records.note: 35:28 also permits return after the high priest's death and 35:27 frees the avenger from liability outside the city; neither is a prohibition, so not mixed.

records.title: Congregation: return the accidental killer to the city of refuge
records.form_basis: "restore him to the city of refuge" (35:25)

records.title: Do not accept ransom for a condemned murderer
records.form_basis: "shall not accept a ransom for a life" (35:31)
records.note: 'He shall surely be put to death' restates the murder penalty as the ground of the ban, so the record is not treated as mixed.

records.title: Do not accept ransom to release the manslayer before the high priest's death
records.form_basis: "You shall not accept a ransom concerning flight" (35:32)

records.title: Do not pollute the land with bloodshed
records.form_basis: "you shall in no wise stain with murder" (35:33)
records.note: Forbids bloodshed (Moral); verse 33 makes the killer's own blood the only atonement for the land, tying it to Israel's homicide penalties, so Civil, the site's label, is secondary.

records.title: An inheriting daughter: marry within the father's clan under the tribal-land provision
records.form_basis: "they shall marry from their father’s clan" (36:6)
records.note: 'Let them marry whom they please' grants freedom within the clan limit; the operative rule is the requirement, so Positive.

records.title: Preserve ancestral tribal allotments against transfer to another tribe
records.form_basis: "no inheritance … shall pass from tribe to tribe" (36:7)
records.note: The title is phrased positively, but the verse's main clause forbids transfer; 'shall hold fast' is its stated ground, not a separate duty.

records.title: Hear disputes and judge Israelites and resident sojourners justly
records.form_basis: "judge justly between a man and his brother" (1:16)

records.title: Do not show partiality between great and small
records.form_basis: "You shall not show partiality in judgment" (1:17)
records.note: Mixed: also 'you shall judge the small and the great alike' (positive). 613 match N284 (unlearned judge) is Maimonides' reading of this verse; impartiality fits the title.

records.title: Do not fear human pressure in judgment
records.form_basis: "shall not shrink before the face of man" (1:17)

records.title: Do not add to or take away from the word God commanded
records.form_basis: "You shall not add unto the word" (4:2)
records.note: The closing 'you shall keep the commandments' is a general charge to obey, not a separate operative clause, so not mixed.

records.title: Teach God's words and acts to children and grandchildren
records.form_basis: "you shall teach your sons" (4:9)
records.note: The teaching command is affirmative. Guarding one's memory is a separate direction, and ‘lest you forget’ states the purpose of that direction.

records.title: Do not bow down to or serve the heavenly bodies
records.form_basis: "lest you … be led astray to bow down" (4:19)

records.title: Love the Lord with heart, soul and strength
records.form_basis: "you shall love the Lord your God" (6:5)

records.title: Teach children and speak of God’s words throughout ordinary daily life
records.form_basis: "you shall teach them to your sons" (6:7)

records.title: Write God's words on doorposts and gates
records.form_basis: "you shall write them upon the doorposts" (6:9)

records.title: Swear by God's name in the prescribed covenant allegiance
records.form_basis: "you shall swear by His name" (6:13)

records.title: Do not put God to the test
records.form_basis: "shall not put the Lord … to the test" (6:16)

records.title: Do not intermarry with the specified idolatrous Canaanite peoples
records.form_basis: "Neither shall you intermarry with them" (7:3)
records.note: A conquest-era marriage rule for Israel as a nation (Civil); its stated aim, guarding against service of other gods (7:4), gives a Moral secondary. Moral primary is arguable.

records.title: Do not covet the silver or gold on idols
records.form_basis: "You shall not covet the silver or gold" (7:25)
records.note: Idolatry ban, so Moral; the metal is an 'abomination' like devoted things (7:26), hence Ceremonial secondary. 'Burn the graven images' is a separate provision, so not mixed.

records.title: Do not take the silver or gold from idols
records.form_basis: "shall not covet … nor take it unto yourself" (7:25)
records.note: Idolatry ban, so Moral; the idols' metal is an 'abomination' like devoted things (7:26), hence Ceremonial secondary. The burning command is a separate provision, so not mixed.

records.title: Do not bring a devoted idolatrous object into your house
records.form_basis: "shall not bring an abomination into your house" (7:26)
records.note: Mixed: also 'You shall utterly reject it, and utterly abhor it' (positive). Idolatry ban, so Moral; the object is 'a thing under the ban', so Ceremonial secondary.

records.title: Bless the Lord after eating and being satisfied in the good land
records.form_basis: "and bless the Lord your God" (8:10)

records.title: Do not worship the Lord by adopting the nations’ condemned practices
records.form_basis: "You shall not do so unto the Lord" (12:4)
records.note: Elliptical verse: read with 12:31, as the title does, it bars pagan-style worship (Moral); 12:2–5 ties it to worship sites. 613 match N65 reads it as protecting God's holy places.

records.title: Bring the prescribed holy gifts and vowed offerings to the Lord’s chosen place
records.form_basis: "you shall bring thither your whole burnt offerings" (12:6)

records.title: Eat the prescribed sacred meals at God's chosen place with the eligible household and dependants
records.form_basis: "you shall eat there before the Lord" (12:7)

records.title: Do not make personal preference the rule of covenant worship
records.form_basis: "You shall not do all that we do" (12:8)

records.title: Do not offer burnt offerings at unauthorized places
records.form_basis: "you do not offer your whole burnt offerings" (12:13)

records.title: You may slaughter and eat meat locally, clean and unclean alike
records.form_basis: "you may slaughter and eat flesh" (12:15)
records.note: 613 matches are P, but the provision grants permission ('you may'); P146 rests on 12:21's 'as I commanded you'. Profane slaughter treated as a food rule, though it borders Sacrifice.

records.title: Pour the blood from meat slaughtered for food onto the ground
records.form_basis: "you shall pour it upon the earth" (12:16)
records.note: This entry requires pouring out the blood. The adjacent prohibition on eating it is separately catalogued and explicitly excluded by this record's own context.

records.title: Do not eat the reserved sacred foods in ordinary towns instead of the chosen sanctuary
records.form_basis: "You may not eat within your cities" (12:17)
records.note: Mixed: also 'you shall eat them before the Lord your God' at the chosen place (12:18), matching 613 match P128.

records.title: Do not neglect the Levite
records.form_basis: "that you do not forsake the Levite" (12:19)
records.note: The Levite's dues (tithes, shares in sacred meals) make this Ceremonial; Deuteronomy groups the landless Levite with dependants, so care for him is a Moral secondary.

records.title: Do not inquire into other gods' worship in order to imitate it
records.form_basis: "You shall not inquire after their gods" (12:30)

records.title: Do not heed an enticement to serve other gods, even from a wonder-worker or close relative
records.form_basis: "you shall not hearken unto the words" (13:4)

records.title: Apply the prescribed death judgment to the prophet who entices Israel into apostasy
records.form_basis: court penalty: "that prophet … shall die" (13:6)
records.note: 613 match N26 is the ban on prophesying for other gods; this record is the court penalty for it, which is a positive duty.

records.title: Do not spare the proven enticer to idolatry out of personal attachment
records.form_basis: "neither shall your eye spare him" (13:9)

records.title: Report the secret enticer to idolatry and do not conceal him
records.form_basis: "You shall surely report him" (13:10)
records.note: Mixed: also 'nor conceal him' (13:9), matching 613 match N21; the title leads with the positive duty to report, so the main form is Positive.

records.title: Apply the prescribed death judgment to the proven enticer to idolatry
records.form_basis: court penalty: "they shall stone him with stones" (13:11)
records.note: 613 match N16 is the enticer's own prohibition; this record is the court penalty (stoning), a positive duty.

records.title: Investigate a city's reported apostasy diligently
records.form_basis: "you shall inquire and search diligently" (13:15)

records.title: Carry out the prescribed destruction judgment on the proven apostate city
records.form_basis: court penalty: "you shall surely slay all the inhabitants" (13:16)
records.note: Devoting the city to destruction also has a ceremonial (devoted-things) side; Moral is secondary as this is the penalty for apostasy.

records.title: Do not rebuild the condemned apostate city
records.form_basis: "shall not be built again" (13:17)
records.note: Burning the city and its spoil (13:17a) is a separate positive duty; this record is the no-rebuilding clause, so not mixed.

records.title: Do not retain the condemned apostate city's devoted property
records.form_basis: "nothing … shall cleave to your hand" (13:18)
records.note: Part of the apostate-city judgment (Civil); the spoil is 'devoted to destruction', a devoted-things rule, so Ceremonial is secondary. Moral (idolatry) is also arguable.

records.title: Do not make a mourning bald patch for the dead
records.form_basis: "neither shall you make a bald place" (14:1)
records.note: A holiness distinction for mourning ('you are a holy people'); Ritual purity chosen because the verse concerns rites for the dead, including 'purification rites'.

records.title: You may eat every clean bird
records.form_basis: "Every clean bird you may eat" (14:11)
records.note: The verse permits ('you may eat'); 613 match P150, the duty to identify clean birds by their signs, is implied but not stated here.

records.title: Do not eat an animal that dies of itself
records.form_basis: "shall not eat anything that dies of itself" (14:21)
records.note: Giving the carcass to a resident alien or selling it to a foreigner is an allowed outlet, not a separate duty; the milk clause is separate.

records.title: Set aside the annual produce tithe and eat it at the chosen place
records.form_basis: "You shall surely tithe all the produce" (14:22)

records.title: Use the prescribed silver substitute if distance prevents carrying the festival tithe
records.form_basis: "then you shall sell them for silver" (14:25)
records.note: A conditional procedure ('you shall sell them') for distant households; it works as a concession, so Permission is a possible reading.

records.title: Deposit the third-year produce tithe locally for Levites, resident foreigners, orphans and widows
records.form_basis: "you shall bring forth all the tithe" (14:28)
records.note: A local relief provision like gleaning (Civil, the site's label), but it is a tithe, declared holy in 26:13, so Ceremonial is secondary.

records.title: Release covered Israelite debts in the seventh year without exacting payment
records.form_basis: "you shall release every debt of yours" (15:2)
records.note: Mixed: also 'you shall not exact it of your brother' (15:2). Ceremonial secondary because 'a release unto the Lord' is proclaimed; 15:3's foreign-debt permission is TL-05-15-03.

records.title: An Israelite creditor may collect a foreigner’s debt during the seventh-year release
records.form_basis: "Of a foreigner you may exact" (15:3)
records.note: The verse says 'may exact', though Maimonides counts it positive (P142); the brother-release clause belongs to C1035.

records.title: Give to the needy without hardening your heart or resenting the gift
records.form_basis: "shall not withhold the affection of your heart" (15:7)
records.note: The title is phrased positively, but 15:7's operative words are prohibitions; the positive duty to give is in 15:8 (C1039).

records.title: Do not close your hand against the needy
records.form_basis: "neither shall you close your hand" (15:7)

records.title: Lend sufficient help to the needy brother
records.form_basis: "and shall surely lend him" (15:8)

records.title: Do not refuse help because the debt-release year is near
records.form_basis: "lest there be a hidden, lawless thought" (15:9)
records.note: A heart-level duty of generosity to the needy (Moral); it presupposes the sabbatical debt release, the site's civil framing, so Civil is secondary.

records.title: Provide generously for a released Hebrew servant instead of sending them away empty-handed
records.form_basis: "You shall furnish him generously" (15:14)
records.note: Mixed: also 'you shall not send him away empty' (15:13), 613 match N233; the title leads with providing generously.

records.title: Do not work a firstborn calf
records.form_basis: "shall do no work with your firstborn calf" (15:19)
records.note: 'You shall sanctify' (15:19a) is a separate provision, so not mixed.

records.title: Do not shear a firstborn sheep
records.form_basis: "neither shall you shear the firstborn" (15:19)
records.note: 'You shall sanctify' (15:19a) is a separate provision, so not mixed.

records.title: Eat the unblemished firstborn animals yearly at the Lord’s chosen place
records.form_basis: "You shall eat it before the Lord" (15:20)
records.note: The recorded duty is eating the eligible firstborn at the chosen place. The prohibition on sacrificing a blemished animal explains which animals qualify for that meal. The record does not separately impose that prohibition.

records.title: Eat the blemished firstborn locally, clean and unclean alike
records.form_basis: "You shall eat it within your cities" (15:22)
records.note: 'Shall eat it within your cities' works as an allowance, like game, for clean and unclean alike (Positive is arguable); 15:21 adds a ban on sacrificing it.

records.title: Observe Passover in the appointed month of new produce
records.form_basis: "Keep the month … and observe the Passover" (16:1)

records.title: Do not sacrifice the Passover at an unauthorized local site
records.form_basis: "You may not sacrifice the Passover" (16:5)

records.title: Include the named household members and neighbors in the Feast of Weeks
records.form_basis: "you shall rejoice before the Lord your God" (16:11)
records.note: Including the Levite, sojourner, orphan and widow in the feast gives a Moral secondary (care for the vulnerable).

records.title: Appoint judges and recording officers in Israel’s towns
records.form_basis: "You shall appoint judges and recording officers" (16:18)
records.note: Appointing judges and recording officers is an affirmative duty. The prohibitions in 16:19 regulate the appointed judges' conduct, which is a separate provision from their appointment.

records.title: Do not plant a sacred grove or cultic tree beside God's altar
records.form_basis: "shall not plant for yourself a sacred grove" (16:21)
records.note: The asherah is a pagan cult object, so Moral (idolatry); the rule governs the area beside the Lord's altar ('any tree'), so Ceremonial is secondary.

records.title: Stone the man or woman proven to have served other gods
records.form_basis: court penalty: "you shall stone them with stones" (17:5)
records.note: Mixed: 17:6 forbids execution on one witness ('he shall not die upon the testimony of one witness'); 17:4 also requires diligent inquiry.

records.title: Refer cases too difficult for local judgment to the appointed priests and judge
records.form_basis: "you shall arise and go up" (17:8)
records.note: The Levitical priests sit with the judge to resolve hard cases. The venue and priests' participation do not make the tribunal's referral procedure a sanctuary rite. The adjacent final-ruling and defiance provisions are already Civil only.

records.title: Follow the ruling of the appointed priests and judge without turning aside
records.form_basis: "you shall do according to the matter" (17:10)
records.note: Mixed: also 'you shall not turn aside from the word which they declare' (17:11), 613 match N312.

records.title: Apply the prescribed death judgment to presumptuous defiance of the appointed priest or judge
records.form_basis: court penalty: "that man shall die" (17:12)

records.title: Appoint the ruler the Lord chooses from among Israel’s own people
records.form_basis: "you shall surely set over yourself a ruler" (17:15)
records.note: Mixed: also 'you may not set a foreign man over yourself' (17:15), 613 match N362.

records.title: Ruler: do not multiply horses for yourself
records.form_basis: "he shall not multiply horses unto himself" (17:16)

records.title: Ruler: do not return the people to Egypt to obtain horses
records.form_basis: "neither shall he cause the people to return" (17:16)

records.title: Israel: do not return to Egypt by the prohibited way
records.form_basis: "You shall not return by this way again" (17:16)

records.title: Ruler: do not multiply wives for yourself
records.form_basis: "he shall not multiply wives unto himself" (17:17)
records.note: Kingship rule (Civil); the stated danger that 'his heart turn aside' from God gives a Moral secondary.

records.title: Ruler: do not multiply silver and gold for yourself
records.form_basis: "he shall not greatly multiply silver and gold" (17:17)

records.title: Ruler: write the prescribed copy of the law from the priests' text
records.form_basis: "he shall write for himself this second law" (17:18)

records.title: Ruler: read the law throughout your life
records.form_basis: "he shall read therein all the days" (17:19)
records.note: Kingship duty (Civil); its stated aims, to fear the Lord, keep his commandments and not exalt himself, give a Moral secondary.

records.title: Give the priest the foreleg, cheeks and stomach of sacrifices
records.form_basis: "they shall give unto the priest the foreleg" (18:3)

records.title: Give the priest the first of your sheep's fleece
records.form_basis: "you shall give unto him" (18:4)

records.title: Allow the eligible incoming Levite to minister at the chosen place
records.form_basis: "then he shall minister in the name" (18:7)
records.note: 'He shall minister' sets an entitlement Israel must honour (613 match P36); as the Levite comes 'according to the desire of his soul', Permission is a possible reading.

records.title: Give that ministering Levite his equal allotted share
records.form_basis: "He shall eat an allotted portion" (18:8)

records.title: Do not interpret the prohibited spoken omens
records.form_basis: "There shall not be found … interprets spoken omens" (18:10)

records.title: Do not practice sorcery
records.form_basis: "There shall not be found … works sorcery" (18:10)

records.title: Do not practise divination
records.form_basis: "There shall not be found … practises divination" (18:10)

records.title: Do not purify a son or daughter by fire
records.form_basis: "There shall not be found … purifies his son" (18:10)
records.note: The fire rite on children is pagan worship akin to child sacrifice, which the brief places under Moral, so the covenant-specific label is not followed.

records.title: Do not chant the prohibited spells
records.form_basis: prohibited practice: "or chants spells" (18:11)
records.note: The negation sits in 18:10, whose list of forbidden practices this verse continues.

records.title: Do not practice as a medium
records.form_basis: prohibited practice: "or is a medium" (18:11)
records.note: The negation sits in 18:10, whose list of forbidden practices this verse continues.

records.title: Do not practice the prohibited portent-reading
records.form_basis: prohibited practice: "or observes portents" (18:11)
records.note: The negation sits in 18:10, whose list this verse continues. 613 match N9 names the Hebrew yidoni; the Saints Translation reads 'observes portents'.

records.title: Do not inquire of the dead
records.form_basis: prohibited practice: "or inquires of the dead" (18:11)
records.note: The negation sits in 18:10, whose list of forbidden practices this verse continues.

records.title: Heed the prophet whom God raises up and who speaks His words
records.form_basis: "you shall hearken unto him" (18:15)
records.note: Heeding God's prophet is obedience to God (Moral), not a rite; 'Fulfilled' reflects Christ as the promised prophet (Acts 3:22), not ceremonial character.

records.title: Apply the prescribed death judgment to the presumptuous false prophet
records.form_basis: court penalty: "that prophet shall die" (18:20)
records.note: 613 matches N26/N27 are the bans implied by the offence; the verse states only the penalty ('that prophet shall die'), a court duty, so Positive.

records.title: Do not spare the prophet whose claimed divine prediction proves false
records.form_basis: "you shall not spare him" (18:22)

records.title: Add three more refuge cities when God enlarges your borders
records.form_basis: "you shall add three cities more" (19:9)

records.title: Do not spare the intentional murderer from the prescribed judgment
records.form_basis: "Your eye shall not spare him" (19:13)
records.note: Mixed: also 'you shall cleanse the guilt of innocent blood from Israel' (19:13), the positive aim of carrying out the judgment.

records.title: Do not remove your neighbour's established boundary
records.form_basis: "You shall not remove your neighbour’s boundaries" (19:14)
records.note: The brief lists boundaries as Civil; moving a neighbour's marker is also theft, hence Moral secondary.

records.title: Establish charges on two or three witnesses; one witness is insufficient
records.form_basis: "two witnesses ... shall every matter be established" (19:15)
records.note: Mixed: also 'One witness shall not suffice' (N288); the title leads with the two-witness rule. Court procedure (Civil); 'Unchanged' reflects NT reuse (John 8:17).

records.title: Impose the intended penalty on a proven malicious witness
records.form_basis: court penalty: "do unto him as he wickedly purposed" (19:19)
records.note: Mixed: also 'Your eye shall not spare him' (19:21), forbidding leniency in applying the penalty.

records.title: Israel: do not fear the enemy in the prescribed war
records.form_basis: "you shall not fear them" (20:1)
records.note: War provision, Civil under the brief's tie-breaker; it is not a rite of worship, so it departs from the Covenant-specific (Ceremonial) pairing.

records.title: Honor the prescribed exemptions from battle for a house, vineyard, betrothal or fear
records.form_basis: "the scribes shall speak unto the people" (20:5)
records.note: The scribes must announce the exemptions; for the exempted man 'Let him go' works as a permission, but the record frames the duty to honour them.

records.title: Offer the specified distant city peace before besieging it
records.form_basis: "call ... forth with an offer of peace" (20:10)

records.title: Place the distant city that accepts peace under the prescribed tribute and service
records.form_basis: status: "shall pay you tribute, and be subject" (20:11)

records.title: Apply the stated judgment to the males of the conquered distant city
records.form_basis: "you shall slay every male therein" (20:13)

records.title: Preserve the stated women and dependants from that judgment
records.form_basis: exception: "save the women and the dependent households" (20:14)
records.note: 'Save' marks an exception to the slaying command; read as a required protected status for women and households, so Positive rather than Negative or Permission.

records.title: Take and use the permitted spoil of the specified distant city
records.form_basis: "you shall take as spoil unto yourself" (20:14)
records.note: 'Take as spoil unto yourself' grants rather than requires, as the context note says. War law, so Civil rather than the Covenant-specific (Ceremonial) pairing.

records.title: Apply the devotion judgment to the seven named nations
records.form_basis: "you shall utterly devote them to destruction" (20:17)
records.note: N49 (save none alive) rests on 20:16, outside this text, so not mixed. Conquest command (Civil); 'utterly devote' (herem) adds a devoted-things character.

records.title: Do not destroy food-producing trees for siegeworks
records.form_basis: "you shall not destroy its trees" (20:19)
records.note: 20:20 adds permissions ('you may destroy' trees bearing no fruit); permissions are not requirements, so not mixed.

records.title: Release the captive wife if the husband no longer desires her
records.form_basis: "you shall send her forth free" (21:14)
records.note: The verse's other clauses (no sale, no contempt) are separate records C1114 and C1115, so not mixed.

records.title: Do not sell the released captive wife
records.form_basis: "she shall not be sold for silver" (21:14)
records.note: Selling her would treat a freed woman as property, a wrong in itself, hence Moral secondary.

records.title: Do not treat the released captive wife with contempt
records.form_basis: "You shall not treat her with contempt" (21:14)
records.note: Mistreatment ban within the captive-marriage law (Civil); its moral ground could make it Moral. 613 match N264 reads the Hebrew as enslaving her.

records.title: Do not displace the actual firstborn in favor of the loved wife's son
records.form_basis: "he may not make ... the firstborn" (21:16)

records.title: Give the actual firstborn his prescribed double inheritance portion
records.form_basis: "he shall acknowledge the firstborn" (21:17)

records.title: Apply the prescribed death judgment in the established rebellious-son case
records.form_basis: court penalty: "the men of his city shall stone him" (21:21)

records.title: Bury an executed person the same day rather than leave the body hanging overnight
records.form_basis: "you shall surely bury him that day" (21:23)
records.note: Mixed: also 'his body shall not remain upon the tree overnight' (N66). Execution procedure (Civil); 'you shall not defile the land' adds a purity character.

records.title: Return your fellow Israelite’s lost animal or property
records.form_basis: "you shall surely bring them back" (22:1)
records.note: Mixed: also 'You shall not see ... and disregard them' (22:1) and 'you may not disregard it' (22:3), per N269.

records.title: Safeguard found property while its owner is unknown or absent
records.form_basis: "you shall gather them into your house" (22:2)

records.title: A woman: do not wear the prohibited man's equipment
records.form_basis: "A woman shall not have a man’s equipment" (22:5)
records.note: 'Abomination' and the distinction of the sexes suggest Moral (traditionally under the seventh commandment); some read it as a pagan-cult or separation rule (Ceremonial).

records.title: A man: do not wear the prohibited woman's robe
records.form_basis: "neither shall a man put on" (22:5)
records.note: 'Abomination' and the distinction of the sexes suggest Moral (traditionally under the seventh commandment); some read it as a pagan-cult or separation rule (Ceremonial).

records.title: Release the mother bird if taking her young or eggs
records.form_basis: "You shall surely let the mother go" (22:7)
records.note: Mixed: also 'you shall not take the mother with the young' (22:6); 22:7 permits taking the young. Treated as land-use law; compassion or food-law readings possible.

records.title: Build a protective parapet on a new house's roof
records.form_basis: "you shall make a parapet for your roof" (22:8)
records.note: The Saints text makes avoidance of bloodshed the purpose of the parapet requirement. Maimonides separately derives a broader prohibition against leaving hazards from this wording, which is distinct from this record's affirmative roofing duty.

records.title: Do not sow your vineyard with a different crop
records.form_basis: "You shall not sow your vineyard" (22:9)

records.title: Mixed vineyard seed and yield become consecrated
records.form_basis: status rule: "become consecrated" (22:9)
records.note: Status rule: the yield 'become[s] consecrated' (forfeit). 613 match N216 reads this as a ban on benefit; the record states the status itself, so Positive.

records.title: Do not plough with an ox and donkey yoked together
records.form_basis: "You shall not plough" (22:10)
records.note: Mixed yoking is a separation law, which the brief places under Ceremonial, so this departs from the site's civil label.

records.title: Elders: discipline the husband proved to have falsely accused his wife
records.form_basis: court penalty: "shall take that man and chasten him" (22:18)

records.title: Fine the false-accusing husband the prescribed amount payable to the woman's father
records.form_basis: court penalty: "they shall fine him a hundred shekels" (22:19)

records.title: The husband proved to have falsely accused his wife: do not divorce her
records.form_basis: "he may not put her away" (22:19)
records.note: Mixed: also 'she shall be his wife' (P219), the duty to keep her as wife.

records.title: Apply the prescribed judgment when the stated premarital sexual accusation is established
records.form_basis: court penalty: "the men of her city shall stone her" (22:21)

records.title: Apply the prescribed judgment in the stated consensual betrothal violation
records.form_basis: court penalty: "they shall be stoned with stones" (22:24)

records.title: Apply the prescribed death judgment to the man who forces the betrothed woman
records.form_basis: court penalty: "you shall put to death only the man" (22:25)

records.title: Do not punish the woman assaulted in the stated circumstances
records.form_basis: "unto the young woman you shall do nothing" (22:26)
records.note: Not punishing the coerced victim is a court rule (Civil) resting on justice to the innocent, hence Moral secondary.

records.title: In the stated assault on an unbetrothed virgin, require the prescribed payment to her father
records.form_basis: penalty payment: "shall give unto the father ... fifty silver didrachmas" (22:29)

records.title: Apply the stated marriage obligation in the unbetrothed-virgin case
records.form_basis: "she shall be his wife" (22:29)
records.note: Marriage obligation imposed as a consequence of the violation (Civil), with Moral secondary as the underlying act is a sexual wrong.

records.title: The man in the stated unbetrothed-virgin case: do not divorce her
records.form_basis: "he may not put her away" (22:29)

records.title: Observe the stated assembly restriction concerning the specified genital injuries
records.form_basis: "shall not enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:2)
records.note: The provision sets eligibility for Israel's assembly. Aquinas expressly treats it as public standing, while Maimonides understands entry as marriage eligibility. The verse names no act of worship or sanctuary access.

records.title: Observe the stated assembly restriction concerning the specified parentage
records.form_basis: "shall not enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:3)
records.note: The provision sets assembly eligibility based on parentage. Aquinas expressly identifies the assembly as public, while Maimonides treats this as a marriage restriction. The Saints rendering of the parentage term remains source-specific.

records.title: Observe the stated assembly restriction concerning Ammonites and Moabites
records.form_basis: "shall not enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:4)
records.note: The provision sets assembly eligibility by ancestry. Aquinas reads it as civic admission and Maimonides as marriage eligibility. Neither reading makes the rule a priestly or sanctuary procedure.

records.title: Do not seek the specified Ammonite and Moabite peace or advantage
records.form_basis: "You shall not speak peace unto them" (23:7)
records.note: National policy toward Ammon and Moab (war and government), so Civil.

records.title: Do not abhor the Edomite
records.form_basis: "You shall not abhor an Edomite" (23:8)
records.note: The direct ban on abhorring the Edomite is moral. Its secondary character comes from the adjacent rule about admission to the assembly and the civil status or marriage it governs.

records.title: Do not abhor the Egyptian
records.form_basis: "you shall not abhor an Egyptian" (23:8)
records.note: The direct ban on abhorring the Egyptian is moral. Its secondary character comes from the adjacent rule about admission to the assembly and the civil status or marriage it governs.

records.title: Admit the stated third-generation descendants of Edomites and Egyptians to the assembly
records.form_basis: status: "shall enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:9)
records.note: The rule defines which descendants qualify for assembly membership. Aquinas specifically treats third-generation admission as public status, and Maimonides applies it to marriage eligibility.

records.title: Keep the military camp from evil and indecency
records.form_basis: "you shall keep yourself from every evil thing" (23:10)
records.note: Heads the camp rules (23:10–15): war-camp discipline (Civil) with a camp-holiness character. Phrased positively ('keep yourself'), though in substance it bars every evil thing.

records.title: Leave the military camp when unclean from the stated discharge and return only after purification
records.form_basis: "he shall go forth outside the camp" (23:11)
records.note: Mixed: also 'shall not enter the camp' (N78). The title leads with leaving and washing, so Positive; the brief counts impurity rules as positive.

records.title: Set apart a place outside the military camp for excretion
records.form_basis: "you shall have a place outside the camp" (23:13)
records.note: Camp hygiene, which the brief lists as Civil; the passage's holiness motive (23:15) lies outside this verse.

records.title: Do not return the escaped slave to his master
records.form_basis: "You shall not deliver unto his master" (23:16)
records.note: Asylum rule for escaped slaves (Civil); shielding the fugitive from his master is also mercy to the oppressed, hence Moral secondary.

records.title: Allow the escaped slave to settle in the place he chooses among you
records.form_basis: status: "He shall dwell with you" (23:17)
records.note: Grants the escapee free residence; read as Israel's duty to allow it ('He shall dwell with you'), so Positive rather than Permission.

records.title: Do not afflict the escaped slave
records.form_basis: "You shall not afflict him" (23:17)
records.note: Part of the escaped-slave asylum law (Civil); oppressing a vulnerable stranger is also a moral wrong (cf. Exod 22:21), which could make Moral primary.

records.title: Do not practice the prohibited prostitution
records.form_basis: "There shall be no prostitute" (23:18)

records.title: Do not perform or receive the prohibited initiation rites
records.form_basis: "no woman who performs initiation rites" (23:18)
records.note: Bans pagan cult initiation, an idolatry prohibition (Moral), not a rite of Israel's worship; so it departs from the Covenant-specific (Ceremonial) pairing.

records.title: Do not bring a prostitute's hire as a sanctuary vow offering
records.form_basis: "shall not bring the hire of a prostitute" (23:19)

records.title: Do not bring the stated price of a dog as a sanctuary vow offering
records.form_basis: "not bring ... nor the price of a dog" (23:19)

records.title: A foreigner may be charged interest
records.form_basis: "Unto a foreigner you may lend at interest" (23:21)
records.note: 613 match P198 reads a duty, but 'you may lend at interest' only permits, as the context note says; the brother clause is a separate prohibition.

records.title: Do not delay to pay a vow to God
records.form_basis: "you shall not delay to pay it" (23:22)
records.note: Vow law (Ceremonial); keeping one's word to God also has a moral core (cf. Eccl 5:4–5), hence Moral secondary.

records.title: Pick a neighbor’s standing grain by hand without using a sickle
records.form_basis: "you may gather heads of grain" (23:25)
records.note: Permission ('you may gather') limited by 'you shall not put a sickle' (a ban, not a requirement, so not mixed). 613 matches P201/N267 apply it to hired workers.

records.title: Eat grapes in a neighbor’s vineyard without gathering them in a vessel
records.form_basis: "you may eat grapes" (23:26)
records.note: Permission ('you may eat grapes') limited by 'you shall put none in a vessel' (a ban, not a requirement, so not mixed). 613 matches P201/N268 apply it to hired workers.

records.title: Do not remarry a divorced former wife after her intervening marriage
records.form_basis: "former husband ... may not take her again" (24:4)
records.note: Operative clause is the remarriage ban (N356); P213/P222 rest on the case's conditions (24:1–3). Divorce law (Civil) with a sexual-purity character ('abomination', 'defiled').

records.title: Exempt the newly married man from war and other imposed duty for one year
records.form_basis: "he shall not go forth unto war" (24:5)
records.note: The title says 'exempt', but the verse's operative words forbid sending him to war or laying duty on him (N311), so Negative.

records.title: Newly married husband: gladden your wife during the prescribed year at home
records.form_basis: "shall gladden his wife whom he has taken" (24:5)
records.note: The year at home is a civil exemption (Civil); its stated purpose, gladdening his wife, is a duty of marital love (Moral secondary).

records.title: Do not take the livelihood-sustaining mill or millstone in pledge
records.form_basis: "You shall not take a mill ... in pledge" (24:6)
records.note: Pledge law (Civil); 'takes a life in pledge' grounds it in mercy to the debtor, hence Moral secondary.

records.title: Do not enter the debtor's house to seize a pledge
records.form_basis: "you shall not enter his house" (24:10)

records.title: Pay the worker's wages at the prescribed time
records.form_basis: "same day you shall pay his wages" (24:15)
records.note: Mixed: also 'You shall not withhold the wages' (24:14). Withholding a poor man's pay is oppression (Moral); the same-day deadline is the civil detail.

records.title: Do not execute parents for children's sins or children for parents' sins
records.form_basis: "Fathers shall not die for children" (24:16)
records.note: 613 match N287 is the rabbinic reading (no testimony from relatives); the plain verse bars executing one person for another's sin. Same negative form.

records.title: Do not take the widow's garment in pledge
records.form_basis: "neither shall you take a widow’s garment" (24:17)
records.note: Pledge law (Civil) protecting the widow, whose care is a moral duty, hence Moral secondary.

records.title: Do not pervert the judgment of the sojourner, orphan or widow
records.form_basis: "You shall not pervert the judgment" (24:17)
records.note: Justice for the vulnerable as a duty (Moral; cf. Deut 27:19); it concerns judgment in court, hence Civil secondary.

records.title: Do not return for a forgotten harvest sheaf
records.form_basis: "you shall not return to take it" (24:19)
records.note: Mixed: also 'It shall be for the poor...' (P122), assigning the forgotten sheaf to the poor.

records.title: Do not glean the remaining olives after the first gathering
records.form_basis: "you shall not return to glean what remains" (24:20)
records.note: Mixed: also 'It shall be for the sojourner...', assigning what remains to the poor.

records.title: Give lashes under judicial supervision in proportion to the offense, with a maximum of forty
records.form_basis: court penalty: "they shall scourge him before them" (25:2)
records.note: Mixed: also 'shall not add thereto' (25:3; N300), the forty-stripe limit.

records.title: Do not muzzle the ox while it threshes
records.form_basis: "You shall not muzzle an ox" (25:4)
records.note: Agricultural rule for Israel (Civil); the NT applies its principle to workers' pay (1 Cor 9:9), the moral character behind the 'Unchanged' label.

records.title: The childless widow in the stated levirate case: do not marry outside the prescribed kinship
records.form_basis: "shall not be married outside unto a man" (25:5)

records.title: The surviving brother in the stated levirate case: undertake the prescribed marriage duty
records.form_basis: "Her husband’s brother shall go in unto her" (25:5)

records.title: Establish the child of the levirate marriage in the deceased brother's name
records.form_basis: status rule: "established in the name of the dead" (25:6)

records.title: Apply the prescribed household designation after the levirate refusal
records.form_basis: status rule: "his name shall be called in Israel" (25:10)
records.note: Public designation imposed after the levirate refusal; a status consequence, so Positive.

records.title: Apply the prescribed penalty in the stated genital-seizure case
records.form_basis: court penalty: "you shall cut off her hand" (25:12)
records.note: Mixed: also 'your eye shall not spare her' (N293). P247 (rescuing the pursued) is the rabbinic reading; the verse states a penalty.

records.title: Do not keep differing sets of weights or measures
records.form_basis: "You shall not have ... differing weights" (25:13)

records.title: Do not accept payment to kill an innocent person
records.form_basis: curse: "Cursed is he who takes a bribe" (27:25)
records.note: Curse formula read as a prohibition; the people's 'So be it' is the covenant-ceremony response, not a separate standing provision.
